confirmed.title: GT estimator-error anchor (−2·err_ip, unclamped) creates a 'terminate fast' optimum and is the likely source of the step-100 value_loss=269k explosion
confirmed.evidence: peregrine_racing_inc8.py:423 `gt = R8.gt_estimerr_anchor(err_ip, self._inc8w.estimerr)` with estimerr=2.0 default (inc8_reward.py:44), err_ip = raw `torch.hypot(e_g[0], e_g[1])` with NO clamp (inc8_estimator_emul.py:798-804). Fixes are hard-zero outside range [9,35] m and band-passed to [12,28] (inc8_estimator_emul.py:176-182); blackout <4.3 m. KF drift under 0.3 m/s² accel noise: sigma_p(t)=sqrt(q·t³/3) = 0.09 m @2 s, 0.47 m @6 s, 1.3 m @12 s, 8 m @40 s (verified numerically). A hovering/lost env therefore accrues −2·err_ip → −0.2 to −16/step, i.e. episode returns of −100s to −1000s; with value_weight=2 and critic_grad_norm=null (UNBOUNDED, resolved config) this matches the value_loss 617→269,156 spike at step 100 when multi_gate first exposes >28 m no-fix legs and post-collapse loitering. Economics: hover 1200 steps ≈ −264 to −7000 undiscounted; deliberate wide miss (T2, −15 terminal, peregrine_racing.py:339) ends the drain immediately and dominates. The docstring claim 'ending early never beats staying alive productively' (peregrine_racing.py:116-121) was written for the R1-dense reward and is FALSE once progress=0 and GT is on.
confirmed.impact: Every step alive costs money the policy largely cannot control (drift is noise-driven when blind); the rational policy ends episodes ASAP (miss/OOB) instead of racing. Also injects enormous return variance across spawn/fix regimes → critic destabilization → advantage corruption → the observed collapse.
confirmed.recommendation: Clamp the anchor (e.g. −2·min(err_ip, 0.5 m) ≈ −1/step cap), or gate it to the fixable band / to fix-fed states, and set critic_grad_norm (e.g. 1.0). Re-run multi_gate; expect the value_loss spike to vanish and episode lengths to stop cratering.
confirmed.corrected: Finding stands as written. Two strengthening corrections: (1) the terminate-fast optimum is not limited to hovering/lost envs — at gamma=0.99 even a well-tracking env (err_ip≈0.15 m, gate every 2.4 s) has continuation value ≈ −23 vs −15 for an immediate miss, so early termination strictly dominates racing throughout multi_gate; (2) a fully-blind 40 s episode's expected GT drain is ≈ −9,600 (larger than the stated −7,000 bound).

confirmed.title: Next-gate obs channels [13:17] are identically ZERO throughout stages 1-3 (G=1), so their first-layer weights stay at random init, then get hit with 24-38 m inputs at multi_gate with no obs normalization
confirmed.evidence: Stages hover/single_gate/blackout_pass set course_n_gates=1 (vq2_curriculum.py:38,49,60-ish; STAGES dicts). With G=1, rel_tables' `torch.roll(gate_pos, 1, dims=1)` is the identity (verified: roll on a size-1 dim returns the same tensor) → gate_rel_pos ≡ 0 and gate_yaw_rel ≡ 0 (peregrine_racing.py:401-411); obs[13:16]/obs[16] are exactly 0 for all 6000 warm-started updates (peregrine_racing.py:627-628 / inc8 obs path peregrine_racing_inc8.py:262-263). Gradient w.r.t. first-layer weight columns of a zero input is zero, so those columns remain at INITIALIZATION. At multi_gate, obs[13:16] becomes the next gate in the current gate's frame, magnitude 23.7-38.5 m (vq2_like seg_len_m, peregrine_course.py:209), with NO obs normalization anywhere (confirmed: obs built raw in obs_zup_torch, no running-stat wrapper in trainer). 30 m × random weights = large random activations injected into both actor and critic at the exact stage boundary — coinciding with the step-100 value spike. The critic's get_state 3-gate lookahead (peregrine_racing.py:641-656) has an analogous shift: with G=1 all three blocks are clamped to the same gate.
confirmed.impact: The warm-start into multi_gate is effectively randomly perturbed through an untrained input pathway; value predictions and the policy mean are corrupted immediately, compounding findings 1-3.
confirmed.recommendation: Insert a 2-gate stage (or run stages 2-3 with n_gates=2 and only score gate 0) so the lookahead pathway trains before the 6-gate stage; and/or add obs normalization (fixed scale: divide rel-pos channels by ~30 m). Either alone should visibly damp the stage-transition spike.
confirmed.verdict_reasoning: Every checkable factual claim verified independently. (1) vq2_curriculum.py lines 38/49/61 set course_n_gates=1 for hover/single_gate/blackout_pass; multi_gate=6 (line 76). (2) rel_tables (peregrine_racing.py:401-411) uses torch.roll(...,1,dims=1); on a size-1 dim roll is the identity, so gate_rel_pos = world_to_gateframe(gate_pos - gate_pos, yaw) === 0 and gate_yaw_rel = atan2(sin 0, cos 0) === 0. With G=1, nxt = clamp(tg+1, max=0) = 0, so the obs consumes the zero row every step. (3) obs indices confirmed: inc8 path (peregrine_racing_inc8.py:263 -> obs_zup_torch, inc8_estimator_emul.py:155-156) concatenates 3+3+3+3+1 then gate_rel_pos_nxt at [13:16] and yaw_rel at [16], raw. (4) No normalization + plain Adam confirmed on the actual diffaero source on the cluster: grep for normaliz/RunningMeanStd/obs_rms/weight_decay across network/agents.py, network/networks.py, algo/PPO.py, env/base_env.py hits only torch.optim.Adam(params, lr, eps) (PPO.py:31,224) — no weight decay, no running-stat wrapper. Zero input => exactly zero first-layer column gradient => Adam makes no update => columns frozen at initialization. (5) The frozen-random-init chain holds: peregrine_vq2_curriculum.sbatch:84-85 shows hover starts FRESH; inc8_warmstart.py is a weights-only transfer, so the untouched columns carry hover's random init through all ~6000 updates into multi_gate, where obs[13:16] jumps to the vq2_like inter-gate spacing seg_len_m=(23.7,38.5) (peregrine_course.py:209; multi_gate sets no seg-len override). With PyTorch Linear default init (+-1/sqrt(20) ~= +-0.22), 30 m inputs through random columns inject O(several-unit) random pre-activations per hidden unit — large relative to trained activation scales. (6) get_state's 3-block lookahead clamp (peregrine_racing.py:644-645) does collapse all blocks to gate 0 at G=1, as stated. Two caveats that slightly temper the impact wording but do not overturn the finding: (a) the pilot ran algo=appo (asymmetric critic on get_state, not obs-20), so the 30m-times-random-weight injection hits the ACTOR only; the critic's analogous defect is subtler — identical block inputs receive identical gradients, so inter-block weight DIFFERENCES stay frozen at init and the critic's differential response to gates +1/+2 is partly random when the blocks decorrelate at multi_gate. (b) The link to the step-100 value spike is correlational: success peaked (16.3%) during steps 0-100 even though the perturbation exists from update 0, and the 269k value_loss spike has competing drivers (6x gates => return-scale jump). The core mechanism, its magnitude, and the recommendation (2-gate stage and/or fixed-scale normalization) all stand.

confirmed.title: obs[13:17] (next-gate rel pos + yaw) is identically ZERO for all three 1-gate curriculum stages, then jumps to O(30 m) at multi_gate through never-trained random-init weights — a built-in observation-distribution shock at exactly the failing transition
confirmed.evidence: rl/vq2_curriculum.py:38,49,60 — hover/single_gate/blackout_pass all set course_n_gates=1. rl/peregrine_racing.py:401-411 `rel_tables`: `prev_pos = torch.roll(gate_pos, shifts=1, dims=1)` — with G=1 the roll is the identity, so gate_rel_pos ≡ 0 and gate_yaw_rel ≡ 0; get_observations (line 620) `nxt = clamp(tg+1, max=n_gates-1)` = 0, so obs[13:16]=0, obs[16]=0 for every step of stages 1–3. Weights feeding a constant-zero input receive zero gradient (dL/dw = δ·x = 0), so after 6000 updates of stages 1–3 the first-layer columns for obs[13:17] in BOTH actor and critic are still at their hover-stage warm-start values, which trace back to random init (hover also has G=1). At multi_gate entry these channels suddenly carry 23.7–38.5 m vectors (peregrine_course.py:209 vq2_like seg_len) → the networks receive a large random-projection perturbation on every input, on top of the return-scale shift. This is a concrete, code-certain seed for the step-100 value explosion and the actor's immediate degradation.
confirmed.impact: The critic's hidden activations are pushed far outside the trained distribution at multi_gate entry, amplifying the critic shock (finding 1); the actor's behavior is corrupted by an effectively random 4-channel input it never learned to ignore or use.
confirmed.recommendation: Either (a) train stages 1–3 with a virtual/synthetic next-gate channel (e.g., sample a plausible next-gate offset even for 1-gate courses so the channels are live and the network learns to read them), (b) insert an intermediate 2–3-gate stage before the 6-gate lap, or (c) zero-initialize the first-layer columns for obs[13:17] at the multi_gate warm-start so the new channels enter as a no-op and are learned gradually. (b)+(a) also fixes the skill gap (no stage ever taught post-passage re-acquisition). Cheap and high-yield.
confirmed.verdict_reasoning: Every factual claim checks out under independent re-derivation. (1) vq2_curriculum.py lines 38/49/61: hover, single_gate, blackout_pass all set course_n_gates=1. (2) peregrine_racing.py:406-411: with G=1, torch.roll(shifts=1, dims=1) is the identity, so gate_rel_pos = world_to_gateframe(0) ≡ 0 and gate_yaw_rel ≡ 0 exactly; in the inc8 obs path (peregrine_racing_inc8.py:254,263 → inc8_estimator_emul.obs_zup_torch:155-156) nxt=clamp(tg+1,max=0)=0 and these channels enter obs[13:16]/obs[16] raw — no noise, no scaling. (3) No obs normalization exists: remote grep of diffaero network/agents.py, network/networks.py, algo/PPO.py for normaliz/RunningMeanStd/obs_rms/norm_obs returned zero matches (control grep on same files returned output). (4) The zero-gradient freeze is exact: obs feeds the first Linear directly (dL/dW = δ·x = 0 for x≡0); PPO.py:31/224 uses plain Adam with no weight_decay, so m,v stay 0 and updates are exactly 0; inc8_warmstart.py does a verbatim weights-only state_dict load with fresh Adam and no column reinit; hover is fresh random init. Hence at multi_gate entry the first-layer columns for obs[13:17] in both actor and critic are literally untouched random init after 6000 updates. (5) peregrine_course.py:209: vq2_like seg_len_m=(23.7,38.5), so the channels jump from constant-0 to 24-40 m vectors through ~±1/sqrt(20)≈±0.22 random weights — pre-activation perturbations of order tens, far outside the trained hidden-activation distribution, in both networks simultaneously. confirmed.title: Entropy budget consumed by easy stages: actor_logstd is saved/loaded across warm-starts, easy-stage exploitation grinds per-dim std 0.22→0.05 before the hard stage, and the tanh-squashed parameterization then saturates to the floor with no recovery path
confirmed.evidence: Verified save/load: diffaero network/agents.py StochasticActor.save writes {'actor_mean', 'actor_logstd'} and .load does `self.actor_logstd.data.copy_(actor['actor_logstd'])`; inc8_warmstart.py:108 `agent.load(init_from)` → every stage inherits the previous stage's collapsed logstd. Entropy is the PRE-tanh Gaussian entropy `probs.entropy().sum(-1)` = Σlogstd + 4·1.4189 = Σlogstd + 5.676, so entering multi_gate at −6.32 ⇒ Σlogstd = −12.0 ⇒ per-dim std = e^−3 ≈ 0.050 vs fresh init (param 0 → logstd −1.5) std 0.223, entropy −0.32 — a 4.4× exploration deficit at the ONLY stage that needs discovery (multi-gate turns, 28–38 m acquisition). The floor: logstd = −5 + 3.5·(tanh(p)+1) (agents.py LOG_STD_MIN=−5), entropy floor −14.32; observed −13.676 exactly constant from ~step 1500 = Σlogstd −19.35, per-dim −4.84, std 0.008 — the tanh gradient factor (1−tanh²) there is ~0.1-0.2, so both the entropy bonus and any recovery gradient are throttled: the run is dead but burns 500 more updates. Root driver: 2000 fixed updates/stage on stages that hit 99%+ within a fraction of the budget — post-convergence updates only exploit (shrink std).
confirmed.impact: Even with the critic shock fixed, multi_gate cannot discover post-passage re-acquisition/turn behavior with std 0.05→0.008; and the saturated floor makes late-run recovery impossible, wasting GPU budget on dead runs.
confirmed.recommendation: Mechanism-matched ranking: (b) logstd RESET (full, or partial to std≈0.15) at each stage transition is the direct fix — it restores the exploration budget exactly where it was spent while keeping the transferred mean; implement in inc8_warmstart.maybe_warmstart (overwrite actor_logstd after agent.load, one line). Add (d)-style guard: early-stop each easy stage on success plateau (e.g., >95% for 200 updates) instead of burning the fixed 2000 — this stops the budget being consumed at all. (a) entropy_weight=0.03 is a blunt global knob: it slows collapse but cannot restore already-lost budget and does nothing for the critic shock. (c) raising LOG_STD_MIN (e.g., −3.5) only moves the floor — treats the symptom; useful as a backstop but requires touching diffaero's agents.py (or wrapping the actor). Also add an automatic abort when entropy pins at floor for >100 updates.
confirmed.verdict_reasoning: Every load-bearing element of the finding independently verifies. (1) Mechanism: /scratch/network/fl3689/diffaero_repo/network/agents.py StochasticActor.save writes {"actor_mean","actor_logstd"} and .load copies actor_logstd back verbatim; rl/inc8_warmstart.py:108 agent.load(init_from) performs the full load with no logstd reset (whole file checked, plus the trainer wrapper peregrine_train_inc8.py) — every curriculum stage inherits the previous stage's collapsed logstd. (2) Entropy accounting: agents.py entropy = probs.entropy().sum(-1) on the PRE-tanh Gaussian = Σlogstd + 5.676, and the squash logstd = −5 + 3.5·(tanh(p)+1) is verbatim; re-derived math all checks: fresh init entropy −0.324/std 0.223; entry −6.32 ⇒ per-dim std 0.050 (4.46× deficit); pinned −13.676 ⇒ per-dim logstd −4.838, std 0.008, above the −14.32 absolute floor. (3) Recovery-path throttle: at the pinned point (1−tanh²)=0.090 — actually slightly WORSE than the finding's "~0.1–0.2" — so dlogstd/dp is ~11× smaller than at init; the entropy bonus (PPO.py: entropy_loss=−entropy.mean(), weight 0.01) does flow gradient to logstd, but the empirically-constant entropy over ~500 updates confirms no recovery occurred in practice. (4) No confound: the only other code touching logstd (inc8_noise_anneal clamp) resolves to None when its keys are unset, and the curriculum sbatch sets none — the collapse is learned exploitation, not a clamp artifact. (5) Root driver confirmed: sbatch NUPD=2000 fixed per stage with FLIGHTCHECK that only aborts on failure (never early-stops converged stages), so 99%+ stages burn the remaining budget in pure exploitation. Independent corroboration: peregrine_vq2_curriculum.sbatch:44-48 comment documents the same multi_gate log_std saturation, and inc8_noise_anneal.py's docstring records a precedent (rc1 saturated two action channels). The only imprecision found — tanh gradient factor 0.090 vs the claimed "~0.1–0.2" — errs in the direction that strengthens the finding. Severity=high is fair: the 4.4× exploration deficit lands exactly at the only stage requiring discovery, and the recommendation (logstd reset at stage transitions + success-plateau early stop) is mechanism-matched.

confirmed.title: No dense along-track drive in random-course mode: R1 is zeroed, R1' is confirmed inert, through-centering is cross-track-only, and R5' pays ≤~0.5/m only inside 12–28 m while pointing — leaving a reward desert exactly where multi_gate segments start (28–38.5 m, where look-at is also OFF)
confirmed.evidence: Verified R1' inert: peregrine_racing_inc8.py:162-163 `self._refline = None if self._random_course else ...`; :345-350 s_prev = zeros, s_curr = s_prev ⇒ r1p ≡ 0; :413 `w_frozen = replace(self.rw, progress=0.0)` zeroes inc7's R1 distance-progress (10/m). What remains as forward drive: (i) R5' `perception_reward` (inc8_reward.py:141-153) = 0.5·w_term·v·max(Δd2g,0)·in_image — Δd2g IS the gate-approach delta (peregrine_racing_inc8.py:429, so R5'/fix_bonus are NOT zero-gated — that part of the concern is refuted), but w_term is a band-pass peaking in [12,28] m with floor w0=0.05 outside (inc8_reward.py:58-62,127-138), giving ≤0.025/m beyond 28 m; (ii) through_centering 10·(prev_ip−curr_ip) (inc8_reward.py:233-250) is the IN-PLANE distance to the target gate's centre LINE — hypot(y,z) in the gate frame — which pays nothing for advancing ALONG the line; (iii) sparse passage +10 discounted by γ^Δt: at 0.99^(300 steps) ≈ 0.05 ⇒ worth +0.5 one gate back. vq2_like seg_len (23.7,38.5) (peregrine_course.py:209) and lookat_r_hi=30 (sbatch line 59) mean a fresh segment >30 m starts with look-at disengaged, R5' at floor, and only the lateral tc pull. Single-gate stages passed 99% despite this (short courses + 70% near-gate spawns), which masked the hole until multi_gate.
confirmed.impact: Between gates the policy flies a near-reward-free desert with sparse terms discounted to noise level — the multi-gate task offers almost no gradient toward the next gate even for a healthy critic/policy, capping recoverability and final lap speed.
confirmed.recommendation: Restore a dense per-env along-track term: simplest is to un-zero inc7's R1 distance-to-gate-centre progress (it needs no reference line and is already per-env; its known wide-line bias is acceptable for the slow curriculum), or build per-env polyline reference lines (Option A seam already exists at peregrine_racing_inc8.py:162). Additionally widen lookat_r_hi to ≥ the max segment length (38.5+) and consider widening perc_r_hi or raising w0 so acquisition of a far next gate is paid. Expected effect: dense gradient across the full segment; this is complementary to (not a substitute for) fixing the critic shock.
confirmed.verdict_reasoning: Independently re-read every cited file and line; all citations are accurate. (1) R1' is provably inert in random-course mode: peregrine_racing_inc8.py:162-163 sets _refline=None when _random_course, :345-350 then sets s_prev=zeros and s_curr=s_prev, so :422 r1p = 10·(s_curr−s_prev) is the exact zero tensor; multi_gate uses course_mode=random (vq2_curriculum.py:73-86). (2) inc7's dense R1 (10/m toward gate centre, peregrine_racing.py:333,364,374) is zeroed at :413 via replace(self.rw, progress=0.0). (3) The claimed remaining forward drive is exactly right: R5' uses delta_gate=(prev_d2g−curr_d2g) at :429 (so it is NOT zero-gated — the finding correctly refutes that sub-concern), but perc=0.5 (default, not overridden in the sbatch) times the band-pass w_term ([12,28] m, floor w0=0.05 per inc8_reward.py:58-62,127-138) gives ≤0.5/m in-band and ≤0.025/m beyond 28 m; fix_bonus=0.0 and centering=0 under REWARD=a. (4) through_centering (inc8_reward.py:233-250, env :443-447) is rw·(prev_ip−curr_ip) with ip=hypot(y,z) in the gate frame — strictly cross-track, pays 0 for along-track motion. (5) Sparse remainder: passage=+10, and 0.99^300≈0.049 checks out (300 steps ≈ one 25-38 m segment at slow speed). (6) vq2_like seg_len_m=(23.7,38.5) at peregrine_course.py:209 and lookat_r_hi=30 at sbatch line 59 confirmed; the curriculum never overrides lookat_r_hi/perc_r_hi, so ~half of fresh segments start beyond both the look-at band and the R5' band. (7) Exhaustive scan of the reward sum (env :406-449) finds no other along-track term: R3 time is a constant −0.02/step, GT anchor (−2·err_ip) and CS (0.05·(c−age)) reward pointing/fix-freshness and are hover-satisfiable in-band (R5' is delta-gated to 0 while loitering), tilt/dact/rate are taxes, spin is a penalty. The reward-desert mechanism between gates is real. Two immaterial imprecisions: the "70% near-gate spawns" figure is actually standing_start_frac=0.3 with airborne spawns at spawn_dist (20,26) m (same conclusion), and the GT anchor does give some dense approach pressure in the 35-38.5 m no-fix slice (accept hard-zero >35 m) plus pointing pressure in 28-35 m — a partial mitigant in the far tail but not an along-track gradient, and far too weak/indirect to overturn the finding. Severity "high" is defensible: the failing stage (multi_gate) is precisely the first stage with inter-gate segments, and the finding correctly positions itself as complementary to (not the sole explanation of) the step-100 value-spike/entropy-collapse.

confirmed.title: multi_gate success metric is contaminated and the 40 s timeout makes a genuine slow lap arithmetically unfinishable — the 16.3% 'peak' is mostly a spawn artifact and the FLIGHTCHECK gate measures the wrong thing
confirmed.evidence: peregrine_racing.py:815-817: non-standing resets (70%, standing_start_frac=0.3) spawn 1 m up-course of a UNIFORM-random target gate (`tg_new = randint(0, n_gates)`); with G=6, ~70%·1/6 ≈ 11.7% of episodes start 1 m before the LAST gate, where drifting 1 m forward = finished = success. So the observed 16.3% peak ≈ 11.7% artifact + ~5% skill, and the collapse to 1-2% means the destroyed policy fails even the trivial 1-m pass (true destruction, not merely 'failed to learn laps'). Lap feasibility: course length ≈ spawn 20-26 m + 5 segments × (23.7-38.5) m ≈ 178 m average; max_time=40 s (base_env.py:40, env.max_time=40, dt=0.0333 ⇒ 1200 steps) requires ≥4.45 m/s AVERAGE — contradicting the slow-lap curriculum intent, so a standing-start lap can essentially never earn the finish/finish-time bonus and 'success' never measures lap completion. The sbatch FLIGHTCHECK (peregrine_vq2_curriculum.sbatch:108-114, success_rate<0.005 AND n_passed<0.1) is satisfiable by the artifact alone.
confirmed.impact: Stage gating and all reported success numbers for multi_gate are misleading; the finish-time reward (T4, +20 + 1.0/s·time_left, peregrine_racing.py:336-338) is unreachable on real laps so it shapes nothing; diagnosis of future runs will keep conflating artifact with skill.
confirmed.recommendation: Raise multi_gate max_time to ~90-120 s (or scale with sampled course length / target speed); stratify logged success by spawn type (standing-start lap-success is the real KPI) — cheap: add `success[standing]` to stats_raw; reconsider the near-gate spawn mix for multi_gate (e.g., bias spawns toward earlier gates or segment midpoints so inter-gate flight dominates the batch).
confirmed.verdict_reasoning: Every load-bearing claim verifies against the code. (1) Spawn artifact: peregrine_racing.py:814-822 — non-standing resets (70%; standing_start_frac=0.3 set at peregrine_vq2_curriculum.sbatch:55) spawn exactly 1 m up-course of a uniform-random gate (tg_new=randint(0,n_gates)); with G=6 that is 11.67% of spawns 1 m before the LAST gate. (2) Success contamination: step() sets newly_finished = gate_passed & is_last (line 696), success = finished (714), success_rate = success[reset] (751) with NO stratification by spawn type — a 1-m drift through gate 5 counts as full success. n_passed_gates ~0.53-0.58 at the peak is consistent with mostly single near-gate passes. (3) Timeout arithmetic: vq2_like preset (peregrine_course.py:208-217) gives spawn 20-26 m + 5 segments of 23.7-38.5 m → mean ≈178.5 m; max_time=40 s (resolved run config; no stage/sbatch override) → ≥4.45 m/s average (≥3.46 m/s on the shortest course) from a standing start under blackout+latency — a genuine slow lap cannot finish, so standing-start success ≈ never fires and the T4 finish/finish_time bonus (RewardWeights lines 335-336, applied line 376) is unreachable on real laps. (4) FLIGHTCHECK (sbatch:108-114 + inc8_tb_trace.py:169-175) gates on the series MAX of success_rate/n_passed_gates vs 0.005/0.1 — satisfiable by the artifact alone; the collapsed run still reads FLEW off its early artifact peak. Two refinements that STRENGTHEN the finding: (a) success_rate is per-reset, and artifact episodes finish in seconds vs 10-40 s for lap attempts, so short artifact episodes are over-represented among resets — the artifact share of the 16.3% peak likely EXCEEDS 11.7% (the '11.7% + ~5% skill' decomposition is an estimate, direction correct; spawns before gates 3-4 can also finish at feasible ~2.3 m/s); (b) 'finish-time reward shapes nothing' is imprecise: it is unreachable for standing laps but pays ~+58 (20 + ~38 s left) for the trivial 1-m drift, actively amplifying the artifact in the gradient. Also note the same contamination applies to stages 1-3 (n_gates=1: 70% of spawns are 1 m before the only gate), so the 99%+ stage numbers are spawn-mix-inflated too. The recommendation (stratify success by spawn type, scale max_time with course length, rebias spawn mix) is sound and cheap.

confirmed.title: Difficulty cliff: multi_gate introduces at least six novelties simultaneously, including obs channels [13:17] going from identically-zero (all three 1-gate stages) to informative
confirmed.evidence: Stage 4 vs 3 delta (vq2_curriculum.py:58-86): 1->6 gates, first-ever turns (sampler heading turns apply only to segments 1..G-1, peregrine_course.py:259-268 — 1-gate courses have ONLY the pad->gate0 segment, so stages 1-3 never saw a turn), first-ever climbs/descents (dz[:,1:] only; stages 1-3 climb 0.5-2.5 m gently), contention stall, ~6x episode return scale (value_loss 617 -> 269,156 at step 100), and long-horizon KF drift (estim_err 0.04 -> 0.5-4.3 m). Obs shift: for G=1, next-gate channels use nxt=clamp(tg+1,max=0)=0 and rel_tables index 0 wraps to gate 0 relative to itself = zeros (peregrine_racing.py:401-411,620,627-628) — so obs[13:17] is IDENTICALLY ZERO for 6000 updates, then suddenly carries the turn/climb geometry the policy most needs, through weights trained on a constant.
confirmed.impact: The warm-started policy+critic face a compound distribution shift on inputs, dynamics-of-task, and return scale at once; the step-100 value spike and immediate success collapse are the textbook signature. confirmed.title: Unbounded critic gradient + lr 2.6e-3 + stage warm-start into a changed return distribution = the 269k value_loss spike that killed multi_gate

confirmed.impact: A diverged critic corrupts GAE advantages for every env for many updates; with norm_adv the SIGN pattern is still garbage. confirmed.recommendation: Set `algo.critic_grad_norm=1.0` (or ≤10) for all stages. (1) Code: remote diffaero algo/PPO.py — both PPO.train and AsymmetricPPO.train (the class GuardedAPPO actually subclasses) clip the actor unconditionally at actor_grad_norm=1.0 but clip the critic only `if self.critic_grad_norm is not None`; resolved config critic_grad_norm=null → critic gradients NEVER clipped. confirmed.title: Discrete warm-started curriculum stages with a compound difficulty cliff, vs the field-standard continuous per-env mixed-difficulty curriculum
confirmed.evidence: Our ladder: 3 near-saturated single-gate stages, then multi_gate adds SIMULTANEOUSLY 6 gates + ±35° turns + a +5 m climb gate + contention stall — success 99.8% → 16% → 1%. Rudin et al., 'Learning to Walk in Minutes' (CoRL 2021, arXiv:2109.11978): game-inspired curriculum assigns each of 4000 parallel envs its own difficulty level, promoting/demoting envs individually on performance within ONE run, with a fraction held at easy levels to prevent forgetting — no staged warm restarts, so return scale and data distribution shift smoothly. This is the dominant practice in Isaac Gym/Lab-era massively-parallel RL (also 'Scaling Rough Terrain Locomotion with Automatic Curriculum RL', arXiv:2601.17428). With 2048 envs we have the parallelism to do exactly this.

However, three load-bearing quantitative/causal elements of the evidence do NOT hold: (1) the clip anchor is rollout-time values fixed across all 32 optimizer steps of an update, so sanctioned tracking is ~0.2/UPDATE per state, not "~0.2/optimizer-step" — the finding states both, and they contradict; (2) the "coordinated drift 0.2x32=6.4/update -> +-650 over 100 updates exactly matching value_loss 269,156" derivation is invalid: movement away from the target beyond 0.2 makes the UNCLIPPED branch win torch.max, which has a live restoring gradient, so the clip does not license one-directional drift — the +-650 match is numerology; (3) the trace itself refutes a hard rate-limit: value_loss recovered 269k->616 in <=100 updates, which a 0.2/update cap could not do (would need thousands) — the cap is soft via shared-parameter generalization, and the spike is more plausibly the warm-started high-value critic meeting early-termination targets (terminal delta = r - V(s) with V carried from blackout_pass) than accumulated drift. Finally, "primary destroyer" is asserted, not established: entropy entered the stage at -6.32 (per-dim std ~0.05), so exploration was already nearly exhausted independent of any critic shock, capping recovery; the auditor's own recommended probe concedes the causal disambiguation vs the entropy hypothesis is still pending. The unprotected stage-entry critic-shock window, all code citations, the critique of job 3295803's non-diagnosticity, and all five recommendations survive; the drift arithmetic, the strict rate-limit mechanism, and the certainty of primary causation do not.

partial.title: Exploration budget: three easy stages consume the state-independent log_std down to std~0.05 before the only hard stage, and the tanh squash makes the LOG_STD_MIN floor an ABSORBING state that entropy bonus cannot escape
partial.evidence: Traces: hover entropy +0.30 (fresh) -> ~-4.1 by stage end; single_gate -> -6.2; blackout_pass flat -6.2->-6.3; multi_gate entry -6.32 => mean logstd ~ -3, std ~ 0.05 vs fresh 0.22, on actions bounded +-3.14. Warm-start carries actor_logstd (inc8_warmstart.py loads actor.pth incl. the logstd Parameter; optimizer fresh but weights not). In multi_gate entropy declines monotonically to -13.67575 EXACTLY constant from ~step 1500 = all 4 dims at LOG_STD_MIN=-5. With logstd = -5 + 3.5*(tanh(p)+1) (diffaero agents.py:58-67), d(logstd)/dp = 3.5*(1-tanh^2(p)) -> 0 at the floor, so the entropy-bonus gradient vanishes exactly when it is most needed — saturation is permanent. The queued entropy_weight=0.03 diagnostic (job 3295803) can slow the descent but cannot rescue a saturated run, and does nothing about the -6.32 already consumed at stage entry.
partial.impact: The hard stage starts with ~25% of fresh exploration std and burns the rest fitting the new value landscape; once saturated the policy is deterministic-bad forever. This makes ANY multi-rung ladder self-defeating: each added easy rung consumes more entropy.
partial.recommendation: Re-initialize actor_logstd (param -> 0, std 0.22) at every stage warm-start in inc8_warmstart.maybe_warmstart — transfer the mean network, not the exploitation schedule; this single change decouples ladder length from the entropy budget. Additionally raise LOG_STD_MIN to ~-3.5 (std 0.03 is useless for control exploration anyway) or add a small floor-repulsion term so the absorbing state disappears. Expected effect: multi_gate retains exploration long enough for the (restored) dense progress signal to bite.
partial.verdict_reasoning: Core mechanism CONFIRMED in code and by re-derived arithmetic: (1) inc8_warmstart.maybe_warmstart -> agent.load -> StochasticActor.load copies actor_logstd.data from actor.pth (verified in rl/inc8_warmstart.py and cluster diffaero network/agents.py), so every curriculum stage inherits the previous stage's exploitation schedule with no reset; (2) the squash logstd = -5 + 3.5*(tanh(p)+1) and state-independent (1,4) logstd parameter are verbatim as cited; (3) entropy bookkeeping checks out at entry: fresh init = 4*(-1.5)+5.67575 = -0.324 (matches trace; finding's "+0.30" is a sign slip), multi_gate entry -6.324 = per-dim logstd -3.0 = std 0.050 = 22% of fresh 0.223 — so "hard stage starts with ~25% of fresh exploration std" is correct; (4) the trainer's noise-anneal (which clamps actor_logstd) was gated OFF, so the collapse is organic. HOWEVER, two load-bearing claims fail verification. (a) Arithmetic: all 4 dims at LOG_STD_MIN=-5 gives entropy -20+5.67575 = -14.324, NOT the observed plateau -13.67575; the plateau corresponds to sum(logstd) = -19.35, mean per-dim logstd ≈ -4.838 (std ≈ 0.0079) — deep collapse NEAR the floor but not AT it. (b) Mechanism: "absorbing state entropy bonus cannot escape / saturation is permanent" requires exact-zero gradient, i.e., fp32 tanh saturation (p ≲ -9, which would read -14.324) — contradicted by the observed value. At the actual plateau, 1-tanh² ≈ 0.09, the entropy-bonus gradient in logstd-space is a constant +1/dim (so the param gradient contribution is constant and nonzero), and Adam's per-element RMS normalization is scale-invariant — tanh attenuation shrinks the policy-gradient and entropy-bonus terms equally and cannot by itself freeze the parameter. The plateau is a near-equilibrium of opposing gradients (or sub-print-precision asymptotic drift), not a mathematically absorbing state. Therefore the dismissal of the queued entropy_weight=0.03 diagnostic ("cannot rescue a saturated run") is not established — a 3x constant upward gradient shifts the equilibrium and can in principle lift logstd; what IS true is that it does nothing about the -6.32 already consumed at stage entry. The practical severity (exploration spent before the only hard stage; effectively deterministic policy with std~0.008 on tanh-squashed actions; each added easy rung consumes more budget) and the recommendation (re-init logstd at each warm-start; raise LOG_STD_MIN) both survive and remain high-value.

CORRECTIONS: the -13.676 plateau is NOT "all 4 dims at LOG_STD_MIN=-5" (that would read -14.324 = -20+5.676); it corresponds to mean per-dim logstd ≈ -4.84, i.e., 95% of the way to the floor but not at it. partial.title: Warm-started log_std is entropy-exhausted before the hard stage, and the tanh squash makes the LOG_STD_MIN floor a one-way trap the queued entropy_weight=0.03 run likely cannot escape
partial.evidence: diffaero network/agents.py:58-67 (per audit brief): logstd = LOG_STD_MIN + 0.5*(MAX-MIN)*(tanh(param)+1), state-independent, LOG_STD_MIN=-5. Empirical trace: multi_gate starts at entropy -6.32 (mean logstd ≈ (-6.32-5.68)/4 = -3.0, i.e. per-dim std ≈ 0.05 — near-deterministic entering the hardest stage) and hits EXACTLY -13.676 (all dims at -5) from ~step 1500. d(logstd)/d(param) = 1.75*(1-tanh²(param)) → vanishes as param goes deep negative, so once near the floor the entropy bonus has ~zero gradient to pull it back — a documented pathology of squashed-bound parameterizations (PPO-CMA, Hämäläinen et al. 2018, diagnoses exactly this premature std collapse in PPO Gaussians; 'Policy Entropy Collapse in RL', emergentmind survey). Andrychowicz et al. 2020 'What Matters In On-Policy RL' (arXiv:2006.05990): 'performance is very sensitive to the initial action standard deviation with 0.5 performing best' and recommends softplus (not tanh) std transforms. SB3 issue #155 (github.com/DLR-RM/stable-baselines3/issues/155): 'When performing curriculum learning, resetting the PPO policy.log_std between training cycles is useful.'
partial.impact: Three easy stages (99.3/99.5/99.8%) consumed the exploration budget; multi_gate then had std≈0.05 to discover 6-gate turning behavior, collapsed after the step-100 value spike, and re-converged deterministically to a degenerate ~1% policy. Raising entropy_weight without resetting the param fights a vanishing gradient — expected to fail or recover extremely slowly.
partial.recommendation: At EVERY warm-start boundary (inc8_warmstart.py), reset the log_std parameter to a target std of ~0.2-0.5 (param=0 gives logstd -1.5, std 0.22 — acceptable; solve tanh inverse for larger). Longer term, replace the tanh logstd squash with clamp or softplus+offset so the floor is not gradient-dead, and consider a per-stage scheduled std floor (e.g. min std 0.1 for the first 500 updates of a new stage). Expected effect: multi_gate keeps exploring past the transient, which is a prerequisite for any of the other fixes to matter.
partial.verdict_reasoning: Independently verified against C:/Users/Fengy/Downloads/Projects/Anduril/rl/inc8_warmstart.py, rl/inc8_noise_anneal.py, rl/vq2_curriculum.py, rl/peregrine_vq2_curriculum.sbatch, and the actual diffaero source on Adroit (/scratch/network/fl3689/diffaero_repo/network/agents.py). partial.title: No value/return normalization in DiffAero PPO + critic_grad_norm=null: the step-100 value_loss=269,156 explosion is an unprotected return-scale shift at the stage boundary, and it destroyed the policy
partial.evidence: Verified by grep on /scratch/network/fl3689/diffaero_repo/algo/PPO.py: only self.norm_adv (line 44/82) exists — no RunningMeanStd, no return/value normalization anywhere in algo/PPO.py or network/networks.py/agents.py; critic clip only 'if self.critic_grad_norm is not None' (lines 132-133) and the run config sets critic_grad_norm=null → UNBOUNDED critic gradients on a loss weighted value_weight=2. Trace: value_loss 617 → 269,156 at step 100 → collapse of success 16.3%→1-2% by step 300. Standard practice delta: rl_games (github.com/Denys88/rl_games, the Isaac Gym default trainer) normalizes value targets with RunningMeanStd ('if you normalize value...' is the documented default assumption); Andrychowicz et al. 2020 rec: 'check if value function normalization improves performance' and found PPO-style value clipping (which diffaero uses, clip_value_loss=true) NOT recommended ('neither Huber loss nor PPO-style value loss clipping').
partial.impact: Going 1 gate → 6 gates multiplies achievable episode return several-fold; the warm-started critic is wrong by that scale, GAE advantages become garbage for many updates, and unclipped critic gradients at lr=0.0026 blow through the shared training dynamics. The 16%→1% collapse coincides exactly with this spike — this is the proximate mechanism of the multi_gate failure alongside the entropy exhaustion.
partial.recommendation: Add return/value normalization (running mean-std of value targets, rl_games-style) to the PPO/APPO path, set critic_grad_norm to ~1.0 like the actor, and add a critic-only warmup at each warm-start (freeze actor or zero actor lr for the first ~50-100 updates so the critic re-fits the new return scale before advantages drive policy updates). Expected effect: eliminates the boundary value-loss cliff; this plus the log_std reset directly targets the observed collapse.
partial.verdict_reasoning: Factual substrate CONFIRMED by independent grep of /scratch/network/fl3689/diffaero_repo/algo/PPO.py and network/agents.py: no RunningMeanStd or return/value normalization anywhere (only norm_adv); critic grad clip gated on 'is not None' and config sets critic_grad_norm=null, so critic grads are unbounded on a value_weight=2 loss; the run's algo=appo maps to GuardedAPPO(AsymmetricPPO) (rl/peregrine_train_inc8.py:118-143) which uses the identical un-normalized value-loss code (PPO.py:290-311). But the causal story fails at three points. (1) The 'return-scale shift at the stage boundary' mechanism is contradicted by the trace: value_loss at step 0 was 617 — normal, indistinguishable from the later 200-1200 steady state. A warm-started critic wrong by a several-fold return scale would show huge loss on the FIRST updates of the new stage, not 100 updates later. The spike is a mid-training transient, and the 'several-fold return' premise is itself unverified (multi_gate is course_mode=random, where the progress reward is suspected INERT). (2) 'Unclipped critic gradients blow through the shared training dynamics' is wrong: agents.py:195-213 shows StochasticAsymmetricActorCriticV builds fully separate actor (obs_dim=20) and critic (state_dim=37) networks — no shared parameters, per-param Adam, so critic explosion cannot touch actor weights; the only pathway is advantage quality, which is insulated by norm_adv (scale) and ratio clipping (per-update step size). (3) 'Destroyed the policy' over-attributes: the critic recovered by step 200 (value_loss 616) yet success stayed 1-2% for 1,700+ further updates with a healthy critic — permanent non-recovery is explained by the entropy floor saturation (entered the stage at -6.32, saturated by ~1500), not the value transient. Causality direction is also unresolved: the spike sits exactly where success was collapsing, so it is at least as plausibly a symptom of return non-stationarity from the degrading policy as its cause. Severity 'critical / proximate mechanism' is therefore overstated; it is a plausible co-contributor to the initial 16%->1% slide and a real hygiene gap.
partial.corrected: DiffAero PPO/APPO verifiably lacks value/return normalization (only advantage normalization), and the run config leaves critic gradients unclipped (critic_grad_norm=null) on a value_weight=2 loss at lr=0.0026 — genuine robustness gaps worth fixing (value-target running normalization, critic_grad_norm~1.0, critic-only warmup after each warm-start). The step-100 value_loss spike (617 -> 269,156 -> 616) is real and may have transiently corrupted advantage structure, plausibly contributing to the multi_gate 16.3%->1-2% decline. However it is NOT an unprotected stage-boundary return-scale shift (value_loss was normal at step 0, the first updates of the new stage), it could not 'blow through shared training dynamics' (actor and critic are fully separate networks in the asymmetric agent — the only coupling is advantage quality, which norm_adv and ratio clipping partially insulate), and it did not by itself destroy the policy: the critic recovered by step 200 while success stayed collapsed for 1,700+ updates, which is explained by the entropy/log_std floor saturation (exploration exhaustion carried in from the easy stages).
