plausible.recommendation: Zero the affected envs' _last_geom rows (or a per-env valid mask) in _reset_emulator; pick one tau_stale (0.5) for the whole ladder so the channel's meaning is stable.

plausible.title: Curriculum stage metrics are trivialized by the spawn distribution: 70% of resets start 1 m in front of a (random) gate
plausible.evidence: reset_idx: with standing_start_frac=0.3 (sbatch:55), 70% of resets spawn at `gp − [cos gy, sin gy, 0]` = exactly 1 m up-course of a uniformly random target gate, at rest, with ±0.25 m jitter (peregrine_racing.py:815-834). In the 1-gate stages this makes the majority of episodes a ~1 s hop to instant finish (+20 + ~39 finish_time), so the 99.3/99.5/99.8% stage successes certify almost nothing about approach, pointing, or blind-zone coasting; in multi_gate it means ~11.7% of episodes are +60 freebies at gate-5 spawns while the FLIGHTCHECK 'FLEW' verdict (sbatch:108-114) can be met by only ever converting the spawn-adjacent gate.
plausible.impact: The ladder's gates pass without the intended skills being learned, so the difficulty cliff is deferred entirely to multi_gate — where four other pathologies (findings 1-4) fire simultaneously and un-diagnosably.
plausible.recommendation: For the single-gate stages, spawn predominantly at standing/approach distance (raise standing_start_frac or spawn 10-25 m up-course); report per-spawn-distance success in the TB trace so stage gates measure the skill the stage exists to teach.

plausible.title: Discount horizon too short for inter-gate credit: gamma=0.99 at 30 Hz gives a 2.3 s / 69-step reward half-life vs 150-580 steps between gate passages
plausible.evidence: Resolved config gamma=0.99, dt=0.0333. Inter-gate 23.7-38.5 m at 2-5 m/s ⇒ 142-578 steps ⇒ passage bonus (+10) is discounted by 0.99^150≈0.22 down to 0.99^580≈0.003 at the previous gate — 0.03 to 2.2 reward units, below the dense-shaping noise floor (tc alone moves ±2/step). Combined with l_rollout=16 and λ=0.95 the direct GAE credit window is 16 steps ((γλ)^16 ≈ 0.37 residual weight) with everything beyond carried by critic bootstrap — so cross-gate credit exists ONLY as a tiny critic-mediated signal.
plausible.impact: Sparse gate/finish rewards cannot shape inter-gate behavior; the policy is structurally forced to rely on dense shaping, which finding 4 shows is absent along-track — the two together explain why multi-gate skill has no gradient to grow along.
plausible.recommendation: Raise gamma to 0.995-0.997 for the multi-gate stage (half-life 4.6-7.7 s ≈ one segment at 3-5 m/s); pair with l_rollout 32-64 and a critic grad clip since longer-horizon value targets are higher-variance. Verify with a shaped-reward-off probe (does n_passed grow with gamma alone?). Note gamma changes shift value scale ~2-3×, so do it together with the stage-entry critic warmup (finding 1), not as an isolated tweak.

plausible.title: Value function cannot observe time-remaining although rewards and truncation depend on it (finish_time bonus up to +40, 40 s timeout bootstrap)
plausible.evidence: Neither obs-20 (peregrine_racing_inc8.get_observations) nor the 37-dim privileged get_state (peregrine_racing_inc8.py:284-291; base at peregrine_racing.py:641-656) contains progress/time_left. Rewards: T4 = (20 + 1.0·time_left_s)·finished (peregrine_racing.py:336-338, 728) varies by up to ±40 depending on the unobservable clock, and truncation at 1200 steps bootstraps V(s') (PPO.py bootstrap: nextnonterminal = 1−terminated) from a critic that cannot know the episode is about to be cut — V near timeout is systematically overestimated.
plausible.impact: Irreducible value-prediction variance of order tens across all stages (inflating value_loss and advantage noise), plus a biased bootstrap at every timeout — significant in multi_gate where many episodes time out.
plausible.recommendation: Append normalized time-remaining (progress/max_steps) to get_state — the critic is privileged and deploy-unconstrained, so this is a free, contract-safe fix under algo=appo (state_dim is measured, not hardcoded: peregrine_racing_inc8.py:202). Optionally add it to the actor obs too if a deploy clock exists (obs-contract change, gate behind the sidecar).

plausible.title: Estimator-emulation fidelity gaps that flatter deploy: KF cold-init AT TRUTH (pos+vel) every episode, no IMU accel-bias DR, and truth attitude/yaw obs on a no-mag vehicle whose deployed yaw comes from vision
plausible.evidence: inc8_estimator_emul.py:403-410 initialize_idx seeds x at TRUTH with uncertainty only in P; :672-679 the synth IMU is a finite-difference of TRUTH velocity + zero-mean isotropic noise (imu_accel_noise=0.3, EmulConfig:224) — no bias term, no scale error, so blackout/stall coasting drifts far less than the deployed stack (the live flight logs showed dead-reckoned velocity error growing ~1.8 m/s — MEMORY, ff_owns_horizontal saga). obs[6:9] attitude-vs-gate and obs[9:12] rates are truth (peregrine_racing_inc8.py:256, docstring 'deploy seam: AHRS assumed good') — but VQ2 has NO magnetometer (live-confirmed), so deployed YAW comes from vision with its own error/latency; 'AHRS good' is defensible for roll/pitch only.
plausible.impact: The policy learns to trust blackout coasting and yaw knowledge it will not have at deploy; the terminal blind-zone pass (the stage-3 skill) is easier in sim than in reality — a sim-to-real cliff in exactly the highest-risk phase (gate proximity).
plausible.recommendation: Add per-episode accel-bias DR (e.g., b ~ U[±0.2] m/s² held per episode, added to accel_body) and initialize the KF with a sampled error consistent with pos_std/vel_std instead of truth; add a per-episode yaw-error draw (constant or slowly-varying, ±2-5°) to the attitude channel. All are one-line draws in sample_episode_dr/reset_idx and default-off gateable to preserve byte-identity.

plausible.title: GAE leaks advantage across TRUNCATED episode boundaries (nextnonterminal masks terminated only)
plausible.evidence: diffaero algo/PPO.py bootstrap(): `nextnonterminal = 1.0 - self.buffer.next_dones[t]` where next_dones stores `terminated` from env.step; the one-step delta at a truncated step correctly uses V(next_obs_before_reset), but the recursion `lastgaelam = delta + γλ·nextnonterminal·lastgaelam` carries the NEXT (post-reset) episode's accumulated advantage into the truncated step because truncation leaves nextnonterminal=1. Terminations are masked correctly.
plausible.impact: Advantage bias at rollout steps straddling a timeout reset — small at ~27 truncation events per 32,768-sample rollout, but grows in multi_gate where slow policies time out constantly; a systematic (not random) cross-episode contamination.
plausible.recommendation: Wrap/subclass bootstrap in the launcher (the diffaero clone stays pristine) to mask the recursion with (1 − reset) while keeping the delta's terminated-only mask — a ~3-line override in GuardedPPO/GuardedAPPO. Low priority; do it opportunistically with the other PPO overrides.

plausible.title: Curriculum warm-starts from the FINAL checkpoint, and the 'best' checkpoint is almost never written (save gated on success improvement coinciding with a save_freq multiple)
plausible.evidence: peregrine_vq2_curriculum.sbatch:98 `PREV_CKPT=${RUNDIR}/checkpoints` — written only at runner close() (diffaero utils/runner.py:166-167), i.e., the last-update weights: maximally entropy-collapsed for converged stages, and the DESTROYED policy for a collapsed stage. runner.py:152-155: `if success_rate >= max_success_rate: ... if i>0 and i%save_freq==0: agent.save('best')` — best is saved only when a new max lands exactly on a multiple of save_freq=50, so 'best' is stale or absent.
plausible.impact: Each stage inherits the most-exploited (lowest-entropy) point of the previous stage — worst case for the entropy budget (finding 3); any recovery attempt from multi_gate's own checkpoint restarts from garbage.
plausible.recommendation: Use rl/inc8_snapshots.py (already built) to retain a snapshot ladder and warm-start from a post-hoc-selected checkpoint (e.g., earliest update with success within 1% of max — higher entropy, same competence). Fix or bypass the runner 'best' gating in the wrapper.

plausible.title: look-at gain-warmup is dead config across the whole curriculum: every warm-started stage force-disables it, including hover→single_gate where the primitive turns on for the first time
plausible.evidence: Stages 2-4 request lookat_warmup_updates=200 (vq2_curriculum.py:52,67,84) but all are warm-started, and inc8_warmstart._force_lookat_warmup_off (inc8_warmstart.py:129-143) unconditionally sets env._lookat_warmup_updates=0 on any warm-start. Stage 1 (hover) is fresh but has lookat OFF (g_yaw=g_pitch=0). Net: the 200-update ramp never executes anywhere. The override's rationale ('a warm-started policy already points') is FALSE for the hover→single_gate transition — hover trained with the primitive off, so single_gate gets the full-strength correction slammed onto a never-exposed policy: exactly the regime-change the warmup was built to prevent (module docstring, the 2/3-seed early-collapse).
plausible.impact: single_gate empirically survived (99.5%), so no observed damage — but the config is misleading, and any future stage reordering or gain increase re-exposes the un-warmed slam; also mildly deepens the stage-2 value shock, feeding the same class of transition instability as finding 1.
plausible.recommendation: Make the force-off conditional: only disable warmup when the SOURCE stage had lookat ON (pass the previous stage's gains through the sbatch, or store lookat gains in the checkpoint sidecar and compare). Remove the dead lookat_warmup_updates keys from stages where it can never run, or honor them.

plausible.title: No observation / return normalization anywhere in the stack; raw obs mixes 0-40 m positions with 0-1 confidences into a [256,128] MLP at lr 0.0026
plausible.evidence: Grep over diffaero script/train.py, utils/runner.py, env/base_env.py finds no running-mean/std or obs-norm machinery (only a cv2.normalize for display); PPO.py consumes env obs raw; the envs (peregrine_racing.py:623-629, inc8 obs_zup_torch) emit unnormalized channels: pos_g up to ±40 m, next-gate rel pos up to ±38 m, rates ±rate-bound, collective in [0, 3.765], confidence triple in [0,1]. No return/value normalization either (see finding 1's raw-space value clip).
plausible.impact: Scale disparity slows learning, makes the single shared lr fragile, magnifies the obs[13:17] zero→30 m shock (finding 2), and is the root reason the raw-space value clip and unbounded critic misbehave at stage transitions. Fixing normalization would defuse several findings at once.
plausible.recommendation: Add a frozen (constant) per-channel obs scaling in the env wrapper — constants chosen once from known physical ranges (positions /30, rates /3.14, thrust /3.765), NOT a running statistic, so the deploy contract stays deterministic and byte-reproducible; mirror the same constants in fly_rl. Add return normalization (or value_weight retune + clip_value_loss=false) for the critic.

plausible.title: Perfect next-gate map + perfect current-gate frame in training vs noisy surveyed map at deploy (acknowledged; cheap fix available)
plausible.evidence: peregrine_racing_inc8.get_observations sources obs[13:16]/[16] from self.gate_rel_pos/self.gate_yaw_rel (course-generator truth), and the crossing/reward geometry uses the same truth gates; deploy hands Policy 2 a Policy-1 surveyed map with VIO+PnP error. Per the brief this is judged minor by Fengyou; noted for the interaction: the KF fix surrogate injects per-episode in-plane bias ±0.19 m (EmulConfig bias_mag_hi) on the CURRENT gate channel, so current-gate error IS trained against — only the lookahead channel is exactly clean.
plausible.impact: Policy may over-trust the lookahead vector for early turn commitment; miscalibrated trust vs the deployed noisy map costs line quality at gate handoff.
plausible.recommendation: Cheap: per-episode additive noise draw on gate_rel_pos/gate_yaw_rel obs channels only (e.g., ±0.3 m / ±3° held per episode-gate) at reset — one tensor draw, default-off. Size it from Policy-1 map-error stats once measured (open question).

plausible.title: State-independent tanh-squashed log_std is a poor fit for a staged curriculum: no state-conditioned exploration, sticky recovery near the floor, and the entropy bonus is computed on the pre-tanh Gaussian
plausible.evidence: agents.py:58-77: actor_logstd is a single (1,4) parameter squashed via LOG_STD_MIN + 0.5·(MAX−MIN)·(tanh+1); entropy used in the loss is `probs.entropy()` of the un-squashed Normal, not the tanh-corrected action distribution (the corrected logprob IS used for the ratio, so the bonus and the ratio measure different distributions). Near the floor the (1−tanh²) factor throttles both collapse and recovery gradients symmetrically, producing the observed frozen −13.676 equilibrium.
plausible.impact: Exploration cannot concentrate where it is needed (inter-gate acquisition) vs where it is harmful (terminal threading); once collapsed the parameterization resists all recovery levers except a hard reset.
plausible.recommendation: Keep for v1 (matches deployed contract), but add the stage-transition logstd reset (finding 3) as standing policy; if a v2 network is ever trained, prefer an unsquashed clamped logstd or state-dependent std head, and an entropy floor via a target-entropy dual (SAC-style) rather than a fixed weight.

plausible.title: 70% of resets spawn at rest 1 m up-course of a random gate: mid-course spawns DO exist (no gate-0 bottleneck), but the 1 m at-rest placement is inside the blackout, below the fix band, trivially passable, and mismatched to arrival states
plausible.evidence: peregrine_racing.py:814-828: `standing = rand < standing_start_frac (0.3)`, `tg_new = randint(0, n_gates)`, non-standing spawn `near_pos = gp - 1m along exit dir` at gate-center height, at rest, tail-first. So later-gate skills ARE trained without surviving gates 0..k (the question's feared bottleneck is absent) and target_gates initializes to the spawn gate. But: 1 m < 4.3 m blackout and < the 9 m fix-accept hard-zero, and the KF was just cold-initialized AT TRUTH (peregrine_racing_inc8.py:223-241), so the spawn gate is passed blind-but-perfectly-informed within a few steps — a free +1 npg and, for tg=n_gates-1, a free success. On the 6-gate stage that alone yields a ~0.7/6 ~= 11.7% trivial success baseline, so the reported 16.3% peak is barely above trivial and the collapse to 1-2% means even 1-m drift-through was lost. In 1-gate stages (tg forced 0) 70% of EPISODES are this trivia. Spawning at rest also never exposes the policy to arriving at a gate with speed mid-lap.
plausible.impact: Metrics conflate trivial and real successes (mis-calibrating every stage verdict), the effective per-episode task distribution is easier than intended, and the arrival-state distribution for later gates is wrong (at-rest re-acceleration instead of carried speed) — a transfer gap that grows once speed ramps.
plausible.recommendation: Change near-gate spawns to U(2, 10) m up-course with a sampled forward velocity (0 to ~2 m/s toward the gate, matching the slow-lap regime) and small heading error; keep tg uniform. This keeps the credit-assignment densification (which currently carries all learning, see the sparse-reward finding) while removing the free passes and covering arrival states. Add spawn-class-split metrics (previous finding) in the same change.

plausible.title: The hover stage is not hover: its course_seg_len override is dead code for 1-gate courses, making stage 1 a near-duplicate of single_gate and burning 2000 updates + ~4.4 entropy units on a stage that never existed as designed
plausible.evidence: vq2_curriculum.py:39 sets course_seg_len_lo/hi=23.7/26.0 'short, so it is near-station-keep', but seg_len_m only applies to segments 1..G-1 (peregrine_course.py:262-263: `seg_len[:, 0] = U(*R['spawn_dist_m'])`; with G=1 the `seg_len[:, 1:]` slice is empty). The pad->gate0 distance comes from vq2_like's spawn_dist_m=(20.0, 26.0) regardless. So hover == single_gate in course geometry; the only differences are lookat gains 0 vs -3/+3 (and the lookat barely engages anyway, pointing ~0.4%). Traces confirm: single_gate step-0 success is already 0.99504 == hover's terminal performance; hover itself converged by ~step 300 (0.988) and idled for 1700 more updates while entropy fell +0.30 -> -4.1.
plausible.impact: One of four stages contributes nothing but entropy consumption and GPU time; the intended safest rung (true station-keep validating the action map) was never exercised, and the docstring misleads future tuning.
plausible.recommendation: Either make hover real (a spawn_dist_m override, e.g. 4-8 m, plus the station-keep reward emphasis) or delete the stage and start the ladder at single_gate with a fresh policy — with the logstd re-init fix, starting fresh at single_gate costs nothing. Also plumb spawn_dist into COURSE_SAMPLER_KEYS so 'gate distance' is actually controllable per stage (the knob the stager thought it had).

plausible.title: Fixed 2000-update budgets overtrain converged stages; no adaptive advance criterion exists — and one stage demonstrably got worse with more training
plausible.evidence: sbatch NUPD=2000 for every stage (peregrine_vq2_curriculum.sbatch:39). Traces: hover at 0.988 by step 300 (85% of its budget idle-exploiting); single_gate starts at 0.995 and oscillates 0.97-0.985 for 2000 updates (zero net gain); blackout_pass starts 0.998 and DEGRADES to 0.90-0.92. All the while log_std shrinks (the entropy finding). ~5100 of 6000 easy-stage updates bought nothing or negative.
plausible.impact: Wasted GPU (~10 h of the 12 h allocation on converged stages) and, more damaging, exploration variance ground down before the hard stage — the two costs compound.
plausible.recommendation: Adaptive advance in the sbatch loop: run in chunks of 250 updates, advance when the end-window (last 200 updates) success mean exceeds the stage threshold (0.95 for 1-gate stages) AND the improvement slope is <=0; hard-cap easy stages at ~600 updates. Implementation is cheap: n_updates=250 per chunk with +init_from chaining (the machinery already exists), tb-trace between chunks. Expected effect: easy stages cost ~300-500 updates, preserving both GPU and (with logstd reset) making the extra intermediate rungs from the cliff finding affordable.

plausible.title: multi_gate warm-start has no critic-refit protocol: 6x return-scale shift + KF-divergence episodes hit a warm-started critic with fresh Adam, lr 0.0026, value_weight 2 and UNBOUNDED critic grad norm — the step-100 value_loss 269,156 spike poisons advantages exactly when entropy is lowest
plausible.evidence: Resolved config: critic_grad_norm=null, value_weight=2, clip_value_loss=true, n_epoch=4. inc8_warmstart.py:16-17 deliberately leaves optimizer fresh ('the right choice for a reward re-pilot') but nothing protects the actor during critic re-fit. Trace: value_loss 617 (step0) -> 269,156 (step100) -> 616 (step200), with estim_err 4.31 m at the same step-100 row (KF-diverged episodes = extreme returns); success halves 0.163 -> 0.095 across that spike and never recovers; entropy drops -6.3 -> -8.9 over the same interval (the policy churned against garbage advantages). clip_value_loss with clip_coef 0.2 slows legitimate re-fitting of a 6x-shifted value target, extending the poisoned-advantage window.
plausible.impact: The one window where the hard stage could have learned (before entropy saturation) is spent on critic shock; norm_adv bounds the scale but not the SIGN noise of advantages from a mis-fit critic.
plausible.recommendation: At each warm-started stage entry: freeze the actor for the first ~50-100 updates (critic-only re-fit at full lr), set critic_grad_norm to a finite bound (e.g. 10), and only then unfreeze. Alternative/cheaper: scale down lr for the first 100 updates of a warm-started stage. Verify against the queued 3295803 baseline: expect the step-100 spike to shrink by orders of magnitude and success to hold its warm-start level through the transition.

plausible.title: Lookat warmup contradiction confirmed in code but empirically masked: _force_lookat_warmup_off() slams full -3/+3 gain at single_gate entry on a policy that trained with gains 0 — no damage visible in the trace, because the primitive almost never fires at all
plausible.evidence: inc8_warmstart.py:113,129-143 zeroes _lookat_warmup_updates on EVERY warm-start; its docstring premise ('a warm-started policy already points at full look-at gain') is false for hover->single_gate since hover sets lookat_g_yaw/g_pitch=0.0 (vq2_curriculum.py:41). The curriculum's requested warmup 200 (vq2_curriculum.py:52,68,84) is therefore dead config on stages 2-4. Empirically single_gate shows no slam signature: step-0 success 0.995, value_loss 7.3 -> 21 (mild), entropy -4.11 -> -3.96 — because the correction is gated on t_cam z>0 AND range in [8,30] (peregrine_racing_inc8.py:318-319) and the gate is almost never in front of the camera (pointing_rate ~0.4%, the vision-dead finding). single_gate->blackout_pass and ->multi_gate have identical gains, so forced-off is CORRECT for those transitions.
plausible.impact: Zero measured damage today, but the forced-off becomes a live pathology the moment the vision-dead problem is fixed (a genuinely pointing policy will exist, and the hover->single_gate slam will then hit a policy that never flew with the correction). Leaving dead-but-armed config is a trap for the retrain.
plausible.recommendation: Make the force conditional: the stager knows the ladder, so pass an explicit per-stage `+env.lookat_warmup_updates` and have maybe_warmstart honor a `lookat_gains_changed` flag (warmup respected when the previous stage's gains differ, forced off when identical). One-line rationale fix in the docstring. Alternatively enable lookat (small gains) from the first stage so no transition ever changes gains.

plausible.title: tau_stale 0.1 -> 0.5 mid-curriculum is a real obs[19] semantics shift but currently moot: with fix_rate ~0 the age channel sits saturated at ~1.0 in every stage — still, all stages should use the deploy value 0.5
plausible.evidence: inc8_estimator_emul.py:34 age_norm = clip(t_since_fix/TAU_STALE, 0, 1); :615 reset sets _t_since_fix = 1e3 (cold => age_norm 1.0). Traces: fix_rate 0.000-0.03 everywhere, so between rare fixes the channel re-saturates within 3 steps at tau=0.1 (dt 0.033) and within 15 at 0.5 — either way it reads ~1.0 nearly always, and the policy has learned to ignore it (as it ignores c_inplane/c_along, which decay to floor without updates). The 5x rescale between single_gate and blackout_pass therefore shifted an input the policy does NOT currently rely on — the premise of the concern is empirically false today, but only because of the vision-dead pathology.
plausible.impact: Minor now; becomes a genuine mid-curriculum distribution shift on a load-bearing input once vision engages (healthy 70-120 ms latency reads 0.14-0.24 at tau=0.5 vs 0.7-1.0 saturated at tau=0.1 — tau=0.1 destroys the fed/contended discrimination the channel exists to provide).
plausible.recommendation: Set emul_tau_stale=0.5 (the deploy value) in ALL stages including hover/single_gate — one line each in vq2_curriculum.py. No stage benefits from 0.1; uniformity removes the shift permanently and costs nothing.

plausible.title: Deploy obs-contract break: stages 3-4 train with tau_stale=0.5 but the deployed obs[19] builder is frozen at 0.10 and pinned there by tests
plausible.evidence: rl/vq2_curriculum.py:66,82 set `emul_tau_stale: 0.5` for blackout_pass and multi_gate (and the resolved multi_gate config confirms 0.5). Deploy side: src/racer/estimator_obs.py:92 `TAU_STALE_S = 0.10` is the default for confidence_triple (lines 129-134), and tests/test_deploy_obs20.py:121-124 asserts `TAU_STALE_S == EMUL_TAU_STALE == 0.10` and `cfg.tau_stale == TAU_STALE_S`. Nothing threads a per-checkpoint tau into the deploy path; the sidecar (peregrine_train_inc8.py:165-169) records obs_dim/r5_arm but NOT tau_stale/sigma_ref.
plausible.impact: A curriculum checkpoint flown through the current fly_rl/estimator_obs path reads age_norm 5x too hot: a 0.1 s-old fix reads 1.0 (fully stale) instead of 0.2. The policy trained to discriminate the 0.19-0.55 s regime sees a saturated channel — exactly the discrimination the 0.5 change was made to enable is destroyed at deploy, silently.
plausible.recommendation: Write `tau_stale` (and `sigma_ref`) into the actor.json sidecar at save time and have the deploy obs builder consume it (estimator_obs.confidence_triple already takes tau_stale as a kwarg). Update test_deploy_obs20 to pin sidecar==deploy rather than 0.10==0.10. Trivial now, a guaranteed field bug later.

plausible.title: Curriculum discontinuities stack at the multi_gate boundary: next-gate obs channels are identically ZERO for all three warm-up stages, tau_stale semantics shift mid-ladder, and the hard stage adds 5 new difficulty axes at once
plausible.evidence: (a) Stages 1-3 use course_n_gates=1 (vq2_curriculum.py:38,49,61). With G=1, rel_tables (peregrine_racing.py:401-411) computes prev=roll(gate_pos,1,dims=1)==identity → gate_rel_pos ≡ 0 and gate_yaw_rel ≡ 0, and nxt=clamp(tg+1,max=0)=0, so obs[13:17] is CONSTANT ZERO for 6000 updates of pre-training; the first-layer weights on 4 of 20 inputs are unconstrained noise when multi_gate suddenly feeds them ±38 m values. (b) obs[19] rescales 5x between single_gate (tau_stale default 0.10) and blackout_pass (0.5) — an obs-semantics shift under warm-started weights. (c) multi_gate simultaneously introduces: 6 gates, ±35° turns, the +5 m climb class, the contention stall, AND the newly-live obs[13:17] — while the critic must re-learn a 6x-longer-horizon value. The 16.3%→1% collapse happens exactly at this compound boundary.
plausible.impact: The warm-start transfer the ladder depends on is weakest precisely at the stage that matters; part of the multi_gate value shock and policy confusion is manufactured by the curriculum design rather than task difficulty.
plausible.recommendation: Insert a 2-gate stage (gentle turn, no stall) between blackout_pass and multi_gate so obs[13:17], the turn skill, and the longer horizon arrive before the full 6-gate load. Set emul_tau_stale=0.5 from stage 1 (it is harmless without latency — age just scales) so obs[19] semantics never shift. Optionally feed the true next-gate vector even in 1-gate stages by appending a virtual exit waypoint.

plausible.title: Warm-start unconditionally forces look-at warmup to 0, but the hover→single_gate transition is a policy that has NEVER flown with look-at — the exact 'full-strength correction slams a fresh policy' scenario the warmup exists to prevent
plausible.evidence: rl/inc8_warmstart.py:113 `_force_lookat_warmup_off(env)` runs on EVERY warm-start; :129-143 overwrites `env._lookat_warmup_updates = 0`. Its rationale ('a warm-started policy already points at full look-at gain') is only valid when the SOURCE stage had the same gains — but hover trains with lookat_g_yaw=0.0/g_pitch=0.0 (vq2_curriculum.py:41), so the single_gate warm-start slammed g_yaw=-3/g_pitch=+3 at update 0 despite the stage requesting lookat_warmup_updates=200 (vq2_curriculum.py:52). Stage 2 survived (99.5%) this time, but the value_loss/entropy cost of the transient is unmeasured and the pattern re-fires any time a ladder changes lookat config between stages.
plausible.impact: An uncontrolled action-composition regime change at each stage start; burns entropy/value stability budget precisely when the warm-started critic is most fragile. Also means the curriculum's stated warmup settings are silently not what ran — a reproducibility trap for anyone tuning warmup.
plausible.recommendation: Make the override conditional: only force warmup→0 when the SOURCE checkpoint's stage had identical (nonzero) look-at gains — cheapest is recording lookat gains in the sidecar and comparing; otherwise honor the requested warmup. One conditional in _force_lookat_warmup_off.

plausible.title: KF cold-initializes AT TRUTH (position AND velocity), with uncertainty only in the covariance — early-episode estimate quality is better than any deploy acquisition
plausible.evidence: rl/inc8_estimator_emul.py:403-410 `initialize_idx`: `self.x[idx,:3]=pos_ned; self.x[idx,3:]=vel_ned` (truth), P=diag(pos_std=1.0², vel_std=5.0²) (EmulConfig:222-223); called from reset_idx (line 613) at every episode. So the estimate starts with ZERO error while the confidence triple claims σ=1 m. Deploy: the navigator exports inf until the first fix (estimator_obs.py:149-162 documents the cold-start divergence) and the first anchored estimate carries real acquisition error. Mitigating: spawns are 20-26 m from gate 0 (in the accept band) so fixes arrive within a few steps and the KF re-converges quickly; the age channel does start at max staleness (emul:615 `_t_since_fix=1e3`).
plausible.impact: The policy's first ~0.5-1 s of every episode (including the standing-start GO — the deploy-critical moment) is flown on an impossibly good estimate, and the critic learns early-state values assuming it. Bounded because the fix band covers the spawn, but the 70% near-gate spawns (1 m, inside blackout, NO fixes available) fly their entire episode-opening on a truth-seeded coast that deploy cannot reproduce.
plausible.recommendation: Cheap and consistent: after initialize_idx, add `x[:3] += pos_noise` with pos_noise ~ N(0, pos_std²·I) (and a small vel draw ~ N(0, (0.3 m/s)²) rather than the full 5 m/s prior — deploy starts at rest, velocity IS known). One extra randn in reset. Keeps the filter self-consistent (draw matches P) and removes the free-truth anchor.

plausible.title: Contention stall model (per-step Bernoulli p=0.01) produces 1-step stalls with an instantaneous age jump to the 1.0 s clamp — real stalls are bursty multi-hundred-ms gaps with progressively growing age
plausible.evidence: rl/inc8_estimator_emul.py:717-720: `stalled = stall_u < pose_age_stall_p; accepted &= ~stalled` — independent per step, so P(≥2 consecutive) = 1e-4; mean burst = 1 step (33 ms). And lines 733-736: a stalled env's `_last_fix_age` is PINNED to lat_clamp_s (1.0 s) that same step — the age channel teleports 0.2→1.0 in one tick, then the very next step a fix (p≈0.84) resets it to Δ. Real GPU-contention (A18 evidence: 129 ms detects, backlog growth) starves the detector for many consecutive frames while age ramps 0.25→0.55→1.0 continuously.
plausible.impact: The policy learns that age=1.0 is a 1-tick glitch instantly followed by a fresh fix, not a sustained blind interval it must coast through with growing position uncertainty. The temporal signature of the age channel — the main thing obs[19] exists to convey — is wrong in exactly the regime it was added for. Multi-step vision gaps outside the terminal blackout are essentially absent from training.
plausible.recommendation: Replace with a 2-state Markov chain: p_enter ≈ 0.003-0.01/step, p_exit ≈ 0.07-0.12/step (mean burst 0.3-0.5 s, occasional 1 s tails matching the clamp); while in the stall state drop fixes and let `_last_fix_age` GROW by dt (delete the pin-to-clamp). ~10 lines, one extra (n,) bool state. Couple the latency draw to the same state (contention state ⇒ contention-mode Δ) so rate, latency, and age degrade together as they do on the real pipeline.

plausible.title: No observation or return normalization anywhere in the stack — 20-dim obs mixes ±38 m positions with 0-1 confidences into an unnormalized MLP, and value targets are raw returns
plausible.evidence: Grep over rl/ finds no RunningMeanStd/obs_norm (only quaternion normalize hits); PeregrineRacing.get_observations (peregrine_racing.py:602-638) and IE.obs_zup_torch (inc8_estimator_emul.py:138-159) emit raw physical units; diffaero algo/PPO.py (remote grep) shows no obs/value normalization — only advantage norm (norm_adv) and value clipping. Obs scale spread: pos_g up to ~38, vel ~10, angles ±π, rates ±3.14, conf/age 0-1, next-gate ±38. Critic MLP [256,128] on raw returns.
plausible.impact: First-layer gradients are dominated by the metre-scale channels; the 0-1 confidence triple — the whole point of case-C — competes at 1/38th the input scale. Unnormalized value targets plus value_weight=2, lr 2.6e-3 and an unclipped critic gradient is the fragile combination behind the 269k spike; return normalization would have capped it. This is the most standard missed best-practice in the setup.
plausible.recommendation: Minimum-invasive (no running stats to ship at deploy): fixed per-channel static scaling in the env obs builder (divide pos/next-gate channels by ~20, vel by ~5, rates by π) — deterministic, byte-reproducible, one matching constant in fly_rl. For the critic, add return normalization (running std of returns) or at least critic_grad_norm. Avoid adaptive obs-norm layers unless the running stats are frozen into the checkpoint sidecar.

plausible.title: Spawn distribution vs deploy: only 30% standing starts, and the other 70% spawn AT REST 1 m up-course of a random gate — inside the blackout, off the racing state distribution
plausible.evidence: rl/peregrine_vq2_curriculum.sbatch:55 `+env.standing_start_frac=0.3`; peregrine_racing.py:815-829: non-standing spawns are `gp - 1m*[cos,sin,0]` (1 m up-course), tail-first, v=w=0. At 1 m range: inside blackout_range 4.3 m, below accept_range_guard_lo=9 m — zero fixes available; the gate is passed within ~1 s from rest. Deploy Policy-2 always starts from a standing GO in the waiting room ~20-26 m from gate 0 (MEMORY launch ritual), and is otherwise always in MOTION mid-course.
plausible.impact: 70% of episode-openings are states the racer will never occupy (at rest, blind, 1 m short of a gate), diluting the batch and inflating stage success metrics (a 1 m drift-through counts as success in the 1-gate stages). Meanwhile the actual deploy-critical opening — standing start, 20-26 m acquisition run — gets 30% of the data. Value estimates near gates are trained mostly from a rest-start context.
plausible.recommendation: For the VQ2 ladder: raise standing_start_frac to ~0.6-1.0 for stages 1-3; for multi_gate replace the near-gate rest spawn with MOVING mid-segment spawns (position uniform along a random segment, velocity 2-5 m/s roughly down-course, matching racing states) — this is the standard racing-RL reset and gives the critic on-distribution mid-course states. Keep a minority of rest spawns for recovery robustness.

plausible.title: Perfect next-gate map: obs[13:17] comes exactly from the course generator; the deployed racer gets Policy 1's noisy surveyed map. Injection point verified. Related: the fix-bias DR under-covers the measured vertical error and is perfectly lateral-vertical correlated
plausible.evidence: obs[13:16] source verified: peregrine_racing_inc8.py:263 `self.gate_rel_pos[ar, nxt], self.gate_yaw_rel[ar, nxt]` with nxt=tg+1; rel_tables (peregrine_racing.py:401-411) builds gate i's position in gate i-1's frame from TRUTH gate_pos — so obs[13:16] is the next gate in the CURRENT target gate's frame (question resolved), exact to the millimetre. Reward/termination use the separate truth tensors (gate_pos/gate_yaw at inc8:359-377), so obs-only noise is safe to inject. Current-gate map error is partially proxied by the one-signed in-plane fix bias, but emul:361-363 applies the SAME scalar to lateral AND vertical (`bias = stack([bias_inplane, bias_inplane, 0])`) with mag ≤ 0.19 (EmulConfig:218) — below the measured ε_vert≈0.215 m vertical boresight bias, zero on depth, and perfectly correlated across axes.
plausible.impact: The policy can blind-trust obs[13:17] for pre-acquisition turning/climb setup; with 0.1-0.5 m per-gate survey error at deploy the early turn/climb commitment is mis-aimed and vision must correct late — worst on the +5 m climb gate where vertical error is largest and the vertical fix sigma (0.28 floor) is weakest. The correlated-equal bias also means the policy never sees vertical-only offsets, the documented binding failure axis.
plausible.recommendation: (1) Per-episode per-gate map noise: at reset draw δ_g ~ N(0, σ_map²) per gate (σ_map from Fengyou; guess 0.15-0.3 m in-plane, up to 0.4 vertical) and add it ONLY to a shadow copy of gate_rel_pos/gate_yaw_rel used at inc8:263 (plus optionally to the gate_pos used in obs[0:3] assembly at line 262 — same surveyed map) — never to the tensors feeding crossing_events/reward. (2) Decorrelate the fix bias: independent lateral/vertical draws, vertical range up to ~0.25 m to cover ε_vert.

plausible.title: Forward-fuse-lagged-content vs deployed RewindKF: direction confirmed conservative, magnitude ∝ v·Δ — acceptable for the slow lap, becomes a real (speed-dependent) training bias at the ramp; do not implement rewind now
plausible.evidence: inc8_estimator_emul.py:693-706: fix content = lagged truth pose (`lag_pos, lag_R = self._lagged_truth(d_steps)`), fused at time t via update_position_idx with NO covariance inflation for the motion since capture — the estimate is pulled backward along the recent track by ~gain·v·Δ. Deploy RewindKF rewinds-replays, removing most of that error. Sizing: slow lap v≈2-4 m/s, contention Δ p50 0.35 s ⇒ 0.7-1.4 m content offset, mostly along-track where σ_depth=0.85 down-weights the pull; lateral offset only during turns. So training sees a strictly worse estimator — the safe direction for collisions. The residual risk is behavioral: the policy can learn a speed-proportional LEAD (compensating a belief that lags truth) which at deploy, where belief does not lag, becomes early braking/early blackout-commit — a speed cost, not a safety cost.
plausible.impact: Slightly conservative flight and mis-calibrated belief-vs-truth timing at deploy; grows linearly with speed so it will start to matter (∼2-4 m at race speeds with contention latency) exactly when the speed ramp begins.
plausible.recommendation: Accept for the slow ladder (matches the stated doctrine). Before the speed ramp, either (a) implement a cheap OOSM approximation in the batched KF — inflate the fix covariance by (v·Δ)² along the velocity direction instead of a true rewind (3 lines, removes the systematic pull while keeping pessimism), or (b) a true state/cov ring rewind (heavier). Re-litigate then, not now.

plausible.title: Fixed 2000-update stage budgets with no success-based early stop: easy stages overtrain at 99%+ for thousands of updates, which is what ground the exploration std down before the hard stage
plausible.evidence: rl/peregrine_vq2_curriculum.sbatch:39 `NUPD=${NUPD:-2000}` applied uniformly; the FLIGHTCHECK (lines 104-119) gates only on FAILURE (stop the ladder), never on early SUCCESS. hover/single_gate/blackout_pass all reached 99%+ (presumably well before update 2000) yet kept optimizing; with reward essentially saturated, the dominant remaining gradient on the actor is variance reduction — driving actor_logstd down (entropy -0.32 fresh → -6.32 by the end of stage 3). The entropy-floor finding is the terminal symptom; this is the upstream cause.
plausible.impact: Wastes ~3-4 GPU-hours per ladder on saturated stages AND destroys the exploration budget the hard stage needs. The two easy-stage pathologies compound: collapsed std + overfitted-to-1-gate value function.
plausible.recommendation: Add a success-plateau early stop to the stage loop (e.g. success_rate_max > 0.95 sustained over 200 updates ⇒ advance), or cut easy-stage budgets to 500-800 updates. Combined with the logstd re-init at stage boundaries this preserves both compute and entropy.

plausible.title: Verified-consistent items (documented so nobody re-opens them): camera geometry matches deploy exactly; blackout gates on lagged fix geometry (correct); action-latency DR brackets the measured transport delay; the env sensor/imu config blocks are inert for this obs path
plausible.evidence: (1) inc8_estimator_emul.py:56-61 IMAGE 640x360, K fx=fy=320,cx=320,cy=180 == src/racer/frames.py:74-77 (HFoV 90°, VFoV 58.7° — frames.py:244-251 confirms the fy=320 mislabel resolution); R_camera_from_body is the +20° mount recompute (emul:64-79) pinned by parity tests; in_image (emul:289-293) uses these constants, NOT any diffaero sensor block — the resolved config's sensor block feeds only diffaero's own sensors, unused here. (2) Blackout masks on `geom_fix["range"]` (emul:710-711), i.e. the LAGGED capture range — matches the deployed detector seeing the lagged frame. (3) dynamics DR latency {1..3} steps = 33-100 ms (diffaero_dynamics.py:589-601) is deliberately centered on the S17 cross-correlation measurement of 67 ms (2 ticks) live transport (diffaero_dynamics.py:586-588); rate bounds ±3.14 and max_normed_thrust 3.765 match the deploy sidecar contract (peregrine_train_inc8.py:165-169). Caveat: the 67 ms was measured on the VQ1 build — worth a one-off remeasure on VQ2 build 1.0.3379.
plausible.impact: None — these are the parts of the honesty layer that hold. Listed to scope the audit.

plausible.title: Fix accept probability has no dependence on ego-motion (blur/rate), and fix arrivals are memoryless rather than cadenced — negligible for the slow lap, flag for the speed ramp
plausible.evidence: BatchedFixSurrogate.p_accept (inc8_estimator_emul.py:315-326) depends only on range and in_image; no term for body rate, angular velocity of the gate in frame, or speed. Real detector recall degrades with motion blur at race speeds (Swift and the project's own detector literature). Also arrivals are per-step Bernoulli — deploy fixes arrive quasi-periodically at the detector cadence; the Bernoulli produces occasional 3-5 step natural gaps the real fed pipeline would not, which is mildly pessimistic (harmless).
plausible.impact: None at 2-4 m/s. At the ramp, training will overestimate fix availability during aggressive maneuvers — same optimistic direction as the fix-rate gap.
plausible.recommendation: When the speed rungs open, add a multiplicative accept factor decaying with |ω| and/or pixel-velocity of the gate centre (computable from t_cam and rates already in hand). Park with the moonshot backlog.

plausible.title: critic_grad_norm is null (unbounded) with value_weight=2 and a shared Adam at lr=0.0026 — the 269k value-loss transient is consistent with a critic gradient blowup that nothing bounds
plausible.evidence: cfg/algo/appo.yaml `critic_grad_norm:` (empty -> None); algo/PPO.py:131-133/309-311 skip clipping when None; PPO.py:31/224 a single `torch.optim.Adam(self.agent.parameters(), lr=cfg.lr, eps=cfg.eps)` covers actor+logstd+critic at the same lr (DETERMINATION 2: entropy enters the joint loss at line 124/302; critic lr = actor lr = 0.0026; eps=1e-8; no reward scaling/clipping; norm_adv is the only normalization, applied over the full T*N batch each epoch).
plausible.impact: one bad minibatch (e.g. the first multi_gate updates with 700-scale value errors squared and doubled) can throw critic weights arbitrarily far; the value clip then locks recovery to ~0.2/update — the two together form the observed spike-then-plateau signature.
plausible.recommendation: Set algo.critic_grad_norm=5 (or 1) for all stages. Cheap, zero risk, composes with disabling clip_value_loss.

plausible.title: GAE λ-trace leaks across timeout truncations: bootstrap is correct (V(s') used) but the eligibility chain is not cut, so the last steps of a truncated episode absorb TD-errors from the NEXT (freshly reset, different-course) episode
plausible.evidence: DETERMINATION 3: our env returns only true terminals as the done flag (peregrine_racing.py:707/741 `terminated = collision|miss|oob|finished`, `truncated` goes into extra only; inc8 same at :391-397) and PPO stores next_done=terminated (PPO.py:154-162), with next_values[t]=V(next_obs_before_reset) computed pre-reset (peregrine_racing.py:771-776) — so truncated episodes ARE bootstrapped, no survive-to-timeout penalty (good). BUT PPO.py:61-67 uses the SAME `nextnonterminal` for the recursion: `advantages[t] = delta + γλ·nextnonterminal·lastgaelam` — at a truncation nextnonterminal=1, so lastgaelam carries the new episode's advantages into the old one across the reset boundary (weight γλ≈0.94).
plausible.impact: biased advantages for any env that times out mid-rollout (and for GUI resets); modest in collapsed regimes (most ends are terminal) but systematically noisy for the slow curriculum where surviving 40 s is common, e.g. hover-like stages and any future slow-lap stage.
plausible.recommendation: In GuardedPPO/GuardedAPPO, store `reset` (terminated|truncated) separately and use it for the recursion cut while keeping `terminated` for the bootstrap mask: delta uses (1-terminated), the λ-chain uses (1-reset). ~6-line override of bootstrap(); the buffer already receives everything needed via env_info.

plausible.title: Constant lr=0.0026 with fresh Adam at every warm-started stage — full fresh-training step sizes applied to a converged policy at a regime change (catastrophic-forgetting-shaped risk), no schedule anywhere
plausible.evidence: DETERMINATION 6: no lr scheduler exists in algo/PPO.py, utils/runner.py, or script/train.py (grep 'schedul|anneal' — only the profiler schedule); appo.yaml lr: 0.0026 (high even for fresh PPO with 32k-sample updates); inc8_warmstart.py deliberately leaves the optimizer fresh (documented at :15-17). multi_gate's best success is at step 0-100 — i.e., every gradient step after warm-start made it worse.
plausible.impact: combined with the broken critic (findings 2/6), large policy steps early in a stage destroy the transferred behavior before the critic can produce meaningful advantages.
plausible.recommendation: For warm-started stages, drop lr to 3e-4..1e-3 (hydra: algo.lr=0.0005) and/or add a linear warm-up/anneal in the trainer wrapper (the step_with_periodic_save hook already sees the update index — one param-group write per update). Cheap A/B alongside the logstd reset.

plausible.title: Privileged critic input (37-d, verified) omits body rates, last action, episode time, and all per-episode DR draws — the 'asymmetric critic' is missing much of the privileged information that actually determines returns
plausible.evidence: DETERMINATION 5: GuardedAPPO.build passes env.state_dim (peregrine_train_inc8.py:136-140); PeregrineRacingInc8.__init__:202 measures it from get_state() = base 34 (3 v + 4 quat + 3 gates × [pos_g,vel_g,rpy_g]) + 3 confidence triple = 37 — the '36' in docstrings is a stale comment; 37 is correct at runtime. get_state (peregrine_racing.py:641-656, inc8:284-291) contains NO ω (body rates), NO last_action/collective, NO progress/time-left (yet reward has an explicit time-dependent term: finish_time·t_left, peregrine_racing.py:373-385), and none of the per-episode DR that shapes returns: actuator latency steps (diffaero_dynamics.py:589-601), sigma_lat/bias (emulator), body_radius (contact bands). The critic also receives NO normalization (same raw ±40 m scales) and suffers the same raw-space value clip (PPO.py:292-298).
plausible.impact: value-estimation variance stays high (the critic cannot explain return differences caused by hidden episode variables), weakening the main advantage the appo switch was meant to buy; the anti-damping mechanism ('critic knows the true margin') is diluted.
plausible.recommendation: Append to get_state: self._w (3), last_action (4), normalized time-left (1), latency_steps/3 (1), sigma_lat, bias, body_radius (3) → ~49-d. Critic-only change: deploy-safe by construction (critic.pth never ships), warm-start of the critic across stages needs matching dims so do it together with the other stage-entry resets.

plausible.title: Actuator latency DR of 1-3 control steps with only the last collective in the obs — the policy cannot observe its own in-flight commands, an unidentifiable partial observability for a memoryless MLP
plausible.evidence: rl/diffaero_dynamics.py:573-601 per-episode delay uniform in {1,2,3} steps applied to the action stream; obs carries only obs[12]=last collective (peregrine_racing.py:621) — no rate-command history, no delay indicator. A fixed 1-step delay is inferable from state; a per-episode random 1-3 step delay is not, without action history.
plausible.impact: the policy must hedge across 100 ms of command ambiguity, capping attainable control bandwidth/aggressiveness — matters little at slow-lap speeds but directly limits the later speed ramp (the moonshot).
plausible.recommendation: Append the last 3 raw actions (12 dims) to the obs — deploy-safe (the flight code knows its own command history; fly_rl already buffers commands). Alternatively keep for the slow lap and note it as a MUST before the speed rungs.

plausible.title: Estimator-emulation fidelity is optimistic on the IMU side: KF cold-inits AT TRUTH (pos+vel) every episode and the IMU predict uses truth-derived acceleration with white noise only — no accel bias/scale-factor DR, so blackout/latency coasting is easier in sim than deploy
plausible.evidence: inc8_estimator_emul.py:603-614 initialize_idx seeds x at truth with uncertainty only in P; :668-679 `a_world=(cur_vel-prev_vel)/dt`, `accel_body = R^T(a_world-g) + 0.3·N(0,1)` — zero-mean noise integrates to ~cm-scale drift over a 1 s coast, whereas a real accel bias of 0.1-0.3 m/s² gives 0.05-0.15 m position + persistent velocity drift, exactly in the terminal blind zone where err_ip becomes the pass margin. attitude_noise=0.0 (case-C trusts attitude) compounds this: the deployed yaw comes from vision (no mag) and carries error.
plausible.impact: the trained policy under-values margin/conservatism in the coast regime; the RewindKF-vs-forward-fuse 'safe direction' argument covers latency handling but NOT the missing bias — this is the one axis where training is EASIER than deploy.
plausible.recommendation: Add a per-episode accel bias draw (e.g. U[-0.2,0.2] m/s² per axis, held constant) added to accel_body, and optionally a small attitude_noise (the Q term is already plumbed, EmulConfig.attitude_noise). Cheap, byte-identical when 0.

plausible.title: blackout_range_m=4.3 is redundant: the accept band already hard-zeros fixes below 9 m (guard) and ramps off below ~12 m — curriculum stage 3 ('blackout_pass') tested almost nothing new beyond latency, so its 99.8% is not evidence the blind-zone skill exists
plausible.evidence: inc8_estimator_emul.py:180-182 `accept_range_guard_lo=9.0` with :320-321 `prob * (rng>=9.0)` — zero fix probability below 9 m in EVERY stage, including 'blackout OFF' stages 1-2; the explicit blackout mask at :707-711 only re-zeros an already-zero region (4.3 < 9). Stage 3's only real deltas vs stage 2 are the content-lag latency model and tau_stale.
plausible.impact: misleading curriculum signal: the memoryless-GRU-not-needed conclusion drawn from stage 3's 99.8% actually shows only that latency is handleable; the terminal 9-12 m coast was present (and passed) since stage 1, which is fine, but the stage naming/gating logic overstates what was validated.
plausible.recommendation: No code change needed for training; update the curriculum notes, and if a harsher blind zone is ever wanted, raise blackout_range_m above 9 (e.g. 12) so the knob actually binds.

plausible.title: Next-gate observation shows a stale phantom at the final gate, and the next-gate channel is PERFECT vs the noisy surveyed map at deploy — both cheap to fix in one place
plausible.evidence: Verified the brief's question: obs[13:16] = gate_rel_pos[ar, nxt] = gate (tg+1) expressed in gate tg's frame (peregrine_racing.py:401-411, 620-628) — yes, the CURRENT target gate's frame. At the last gate, nxt=clamp(tg+1, max=G-1)=tg, so the obs shows gate G-1's position in gate G-2's frame — a nonzero ~25-38 m vector implying a phantom next gate on final approach. And gate_rel_pos comes exactly from the course generator (perfect), while deploy hands Policy 2 a Policy-1 surveyed map with noise.
plausible.impact: small systematic obs inconsistency on the final approach of every course; the perfect-map gap trains the policy to over-trust the lookahead channel (acknowledged-minor per Fengyou, but the fix is nearly free).
plausible.recommendation: (a) at the last gate, zero the next-gate block (and rely on [16] rel-yaw=0 as the 'no next gate' sentinel); (b) add per-episode jitter to gate_rel_pos/gate_yaw_rel at reset (e.g. N(0, 0.3-0.5 m) in-plane, matching the expected survey error) — one tensor add in _assign_courses.

plausible.title: Minor trainer footguns (determinations 2/4/6 remainder): entropy bonus is pre-tanh Normal entropy; actor grad-clip covers logstd jointly; torch_deterministic=False; single global RNG stream; 'best' checkpoint only saved on save_freq multiples; nan-guard aborts on CUMULATIVE not consecutive skips
plausible.evidence: agents.py:76 `entropy = probs.entropy().sum(-1)` (pre-squash; logged entropy is not action entropy and is unbounded below); PPO.py:128-130 clip_grad_norm_ over agent.actor.parameters() includes actor_logstd; cfg/config_train.yaml torch_deterministic: False and script/train.py:48-52 seeds only global streams (reruns are not bit-reproducible; env course/DR draws share one stream — benign); utils/runner.py:152-155 saves 'best' only when success_rate>=max AND i%save_freq==0 (a peak between multiples is lost — relevant since multi_gate's best policy existed only at steps 0-100); peregrine_train_inc8.py:70-79 counts total skips but the message says consecutive. DETERMINATION 4 core: actor.pth DOES carry actor_logstd and warm-start restores it (agents.py:79-87) — covered in finding 1.
plausible.impact: individually small; the 'best'-save quirk concretely cost this pilot its best multi_gate checkpoint (peak 16% at step ~100 with save_freq=50 was save-eligible only at exactly step 50/100).
plausible.recommendation: Save 'best' whenever success_rate improves (drop the modulus condition) — one-line change in the runner wrapper; leave the rest documented.

plausible.title: No observation normalization anywhere (confirmed absent in DiffAero) with channels spanning ~26 m positions to 0-1 confidences
plausible.evidence: Grep of diffaero algo/PPO.py + network/networks.py + network/agents.py: no RunningMeanStd/obs normalization exists; audit brief confirms none found repo-side. Obs-20 mixes gate-relative position up to ~26 m, velocities, radians, body rates ±3.14, [0,1] confidences. Andrychowicz et al. 2020 recommendation is unambiguous: 'Always use observation normalization' (one of their strongest findings across 250k agents).
plausible.impact: Ill-conditioned inputs slow critic re-fitting at every warm-start (the largest-magnitude channels dominate early gradients) and make the 128/256-unit MLPs waste capacity on rescaling; hurts most exactly at the multi_gate boundary where position magnitudes and course geometry change.
plausible.recommendation: Prefer FIXED static scaling over running stats for deploy determinism: divide obs[0:3]/obs[13:16] by ~20 m, velocities by ~10, keep angles/rates/conf as-is; bake the same constants into the deploy wrapper. One-line env change, zero deploy risk (byte-id off by default via config). Expected effect: modest but free conditioning gain; standard in every top stack (rl_games/RSL-RL empirical_normalization, SB3 VecNormalize).

plausible.title: Perception objective diverges from Swift's proven form: Swift rewards camera-axis alignment with an exponential bonus and observes gate CORNERS, not center pose
plausible.evidence: Swift Methods (Nature 2023, PMC10468397): observation = robot state (attitude as ROTATION MATRIX, R15) + 'relative positions of the four gate corners (R12)' of only the next gate + previous action; reward r = r_prog + r_perc + r_cmd - r_crash with r_perc = lambda2*exp(lambda3*delta_cam) (exponential in camera-axis-to-gate-center angle) and r_cmd = lambda4*|omega| + lambda5*||a_t - a_{t-1}||^2; crash = 5.0. Ours: euler-zyx attitude, gate-center relative pose, lookat_g_yaw=-3/g_pitch=+3 (linear gains, sign conventions differ per axis), jerk=0.1, collision=10, no explicit ||a_t-a_{t-1}||^2 action-difference term confirmed, previous action only partially observed (only last collective, obs[12], not the full 4-dim last action).
plausible.impact: (a) Euler angles have wrap discontinuities that rotation-matrix (or 6D) attitude avoids — matters once ±35° turns and the +5 m climb gate produce large attitude excursions; (b) corners encode gate size/orientation/approach angle that center-pose+yaw only partially carries; (c) missing full previous-action obs weakens smoothness learning given action-latency DR of 1-3 steps (the policy cannot see what it last commanded on 3 of 4 axes).
plausible.recommendation: Cheapest first: add the full previous 4-dim action to obs (Swift does; also directly helps with the modeled actuation latency). Consider rotation-matrix attitude in a future obs rev. Corner obs is a bigger change — defer unless turning gates stay hard after the critical fixes. Expected effect: better smoothness/latency handling; incremental gate-approach shaping.

plausible.title: Warm-start forces lookat warmup to 0, injecting full-gain perception reward instantly at every stage boundary on top of the task shift
plausible.evidence: Audit brief: inc8_warmstart.py forces lookat warmup to 0 on warm-start while vq2_curriculum.py stages 2-4 request lookat_warmup_updates=200; stage 1 trains lookat OFF entirely, so the single_gate boundary adds a brand-new -3/+3 reward term at full gain to a policy that never saw it, and multi_gate re-applies full gain to the new 6-gate geometry (where look-at conflicts with turning anticipation). Reward-scale discontinuities at transfer boundaries are exactly what curriculum practice smooths (Rudin 2021 keeps reward fixed and moves only difficulty).
plausible.impact: Adds an avoidable reward-distribution shift to each boundary, further destabilizing the critic (compounds the value-target scale problem) and shaping against yaw-leading turns early in multi_gate.
plausible.recommendation: Honor the 200-update lookat warmup at every stage boundary (remove the force-to-0 in inc8_warmstart.py, or ramp any NEW reward term regardless of warm-start). Trivial change; removes one confound from the boundary shock.

plausible.title: Swift's sim-to-real recipe fine-tunes on EMPIRICAL residual noise models (GPs fit to ~50 s of real flight); our perfect next-gate map and truth attitude have no equivalent final noise-hardening stage
plausible.evidence: Swift Methods (PMC10468397): 'We collect three full rollouts in the real world... approximately 50 s of flight time'; fit 'nine 1D Gaussian processes to the observation residuals' (position/velocity/attitude vs ground truth) and integrate them into simulation for a 2e7-step fine-tune of the policy only. Our training gives the racer an EXACT next-gate map (obs[13:16], [16]) and TRUTH attitude (obs[6:9]) while deploy hands it a Policy-1 noisy surveyed map and AHRS attitude — with no fine-tune stage that injects the measured deploy-time error statistics.
plausible.impact: The policy can learn to lean on the perfect map channel (e.g. pre-committing turn direction from exact next-gate bearing) in ways that degrade nonlinearly under survey error; same for attitude under VIO/AHRS drift given NO-mag yaw comes from vision. This is a fidelity gap the winning system explicitly closed empirically.
plausible.recommendation: Adopt Swift's pattern cheaply: after multi_gate converges, add a short fine-tune stage where (a) next-gate map channels get per-episode frozen offsets drawn from Policy-1 survey-error stats (measure them from slow-lap logs once available), (b) attitude channels get the residual model from real/sim VIO comparison. Weights-only warm-start, ~10% of stage budget. Expected effect: robustness at deploy without touching the main curriculum.

plausible.title: gamma=0.99 / GAE lambda=0.95 at 30 Hz is field-standard and NOT a suspect; do not spend budget here
plausible.evidence: Song et al. 2021 'Autonomous Drone Racing with Deep RL' (arXiv:2103.08624) introduced the dense gate-progress reward precisely because sparse lap-time/gate rewards fail credit assignment, making large gamma unnecessary; our progress=10.0 term is that same dense bridge, so gates are not sparse from the return's perspective. Racing/locomotion stacks at 30-100 Hz overwhelmingly use gamma=0.99 (Rudin 2021 at 50 Hz; SB3 defaults in Song et al. 2023; 'Reward design and hyperparameter tuning...' Sci Reports 2025 found 0.99 optimal for racing generalization). Andrychowicz 2020: gamma is the top hyperparameter to tune but 0.99 is the start point; GAE lambda 0.9-0.95 recommended.
plausible.impact: None expected; listed to close research target 4 and prevent misattributing the multi_gate collapse to horizon length.
plausible.recommendation: Keep 0.99/0.95. Only revisit (toward 0.995) if, after the critical fixes, long 6-gate courses show late-gate undervaluation — check via per-gate value estimates, not blind sweeps.

plausible.title: Verify the asymmetric critic is actually engaged and feeding 37-dim privileged state in these runs; rl_games practice pairs privileged critics WITH value normalization
plausible.evidence: Memory notes the historical footgun (algo=ppo left the privileged critic never connected, input_dim==obs_dim==20; GuardedAPPO/appo wired input_dim=37). The resolved config says name=appo, but the multi_gate value-loss behavior is consistent with a critic struggling — worth one log-line check (critic input_dim printed at build) per run rather than assumption. Community standard (rl_games asymmetric actor-critic docs, isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab isaaclab_rl API; RSL-RL privileged-critic PPO) treats value normalization as the default companion because privileged critics fit larger-magnitude targets confidently.
plausible.impact: If any run silently degrades to the symmetric path, the memory-cited 'symmetric=catastrophic' seed-collapse mode returns; even when engaged, an unnormalized privileged critic remains the finding-2 hazard.
plausible.recommendation: Add/verify a startup assertion + logged critic input_dim=37 in peregrine_train_inc8.py sidecar output for every job; bundle with the finding-2 value-normalization change.

per_auditor_summaries.summary: Reward-activity audit of the VQ2 curriculum (course_mode=random, vq2_like, REWARD arm a) confirms the suspected dead-progress hole and finds the multi_gate collapse over-determined by five interacting defects. (1) CONFIRMED: arc-progress R1' is the exact zero tensor on random courses (_refline=None → s_curr==s_prev, peregrine_racing_inc8.py:162/346-350) AND the inc7 dense d2g progress is unconditionally zeroed (line 413) — so NO along-track drive exists at all; with gamma=0.99 (3.3 s horizon) the sparse +10 passage 450 steps away is worth ~0.11 discounted. (2) NOT confirmed dead: R5' and fix_bonus gate on the per-env gate-approach delta on random courses (line 429), not the zero arc delta — R5' (0.5) is alive and is in fact the only dense forward incentive (~0.03/step); fix_bonus is off only by weight; the CS anneal, however, is a dead knob (instant-on at defaults). (3) The unclamped GT anchor −2·err_ip becomes a −0.2..−16/step drain wherever fixes are absent (KF drift 0.47 m @6 s, 8 m @40 s), producing returns of −100s..−1000s that match the step-100 value_loss=269k spike (critic_grad_norm unbounded) and making 'terminate fast' (deliberate miss −15) strictly dominate hovering AND honest leg-flying — the docstring's anti-early-exit guarantee only held while dense progress existed. (4) through_centering (10) is cross-track only but pays a ~+80/leg one-time alignment pot, 8x the passage bonus — funding an align-then-terminate optimum. (5) The collapse is compounded by mechanical warm-start defects: entropy carried to logstd≈−4.84 with tanh gradient attenuated 11x (the queued 0.03 entropy fix will act ~11x slower than expected); next-gate obs[13:17] are identically zero in all G=1 stages (roll-identity, verified) so their first-layer weights sit at random init until 24-38 m inputs slam them at multi_gate start with no obs normalization; and max_time=40 s makes a full lap physically unreachable at curriculum speeds (success structurally capped ≈35%, finish bonus dead, +60 instant-finish freebies at gate-5 spawns inflating value variance). Highest-leverage fixes, in order: re-enable signed d2g progress on random courses (one line), clamp/gate the GT anchor + bound critic grad, reset actor_logstd per stage warm-start, add a 2-gate intermediate stage or obs scaling, and raise multi_gate max_time or score on n_passed_gates.

Causal reconstruction of the multi_gate collapse: three easy 1-gate stages (2000 fixed updates each, converging early then pure-exploiting) ground the saved-and-reloaded actor_logstd from std 0.22 to 0.05 (entropy −6.32 at entry); at the multi_gate transition the warm-started critic met three simultaneous shocks — a new return landscape (6 gates, 1200-step episodes, unreachable finish bonus), obs[13:17] next-gate channels jumping from identically-zero (a G=1 artifact of rel_tables' roll) to O(30 m) through never-trained random-init weights, and fresh Adam moments at lr 0.0026 with NO critic grad clip and a raw-space value clip (clip_coef 0.2 on values of scale 100s) — producing the step-100 value_loss=269k explosion; with l_rollout=16 every advantage is bootstrap-dominated, so 200 updates of unit-normalized random-sign advantages destroyed the transferred policy (16.3%→1-2%, where ~11.7% of 'success' was always a spawn-1-m-before-the-last-gate artifact), and the entropy floor (tanh-squashed logstd saturating at −13.68 by step 1500) then blocked any recovery. Dominant destroyer = critic shock; dominant recovery-blocker = entropy floor; dominant why-it-can't-relearn = no dense along-track reward in random-course mode (R1 zeroed, R1' verified inert, through-centering is cross-track-only, R5' pays only in 12-28 m, look-at disengages >30 m) plus gamma=0.99's 69-step half-life vs 150-580-step inter-gate spans. The queued entropy_weight=0.03 run will not disambiguate; the best single probe is an actor-frozen (critic-only) multi_gate rerun at ew=0.01. Top interventions in order: stage-entry critic-only warmup + critic_grad_norm=1 + transition lr drop; logstd reset at stage transitions + early-stop easy stages on plateau; fix the zero→live next-gate channels (virtual next gate or 2-3-gate intermediate stage); restore a dense per-env progress term and raise gamma to 0.995-0.997; raise multi_gate max_time and stratify success by spawn type so the gate metric measures laps. Secondary: no obs/return normalization anywhere, GAE leaks across truncation boundaries, warm-start uses the final (most-collapsed) checkpoint with the 'best' save effectively never firing, look-at warmup is dead config, and the estimator emulation flatters deploy (KF init at truth, no IMU bias, truth yaw on a no-mag vehicle).

Curriculum audit of the VQ2 4-stage ladder (hover/single_gate/blackout_pass/multi_gate), verified against the actual cluster traces. The multi_gate collapse is overdetermined by three compounding root causes, all confirmed: (1) NO dense forward-progress reward exists on random courses — inc8 zeroes inc7's R1 (peregrine_racing_inc8.py:413) expecting arc-progress R1' to replace it, but R1' is the exact-zero tensor when course_mode=random (no refline), and through-centering is lateral-only; forward drive is sparse pass bonuses densified solely by the 70% spawn-1-m-before-a-gate trick, unreachable across 25 m segments once exploration collapses. (2) Vision never engages ANYWHERE: pointing_rate 0.2-5%, lockband ~0, fix_rate 0-3% in every stage; the 99% stage successes are flown blind on a truth-initialized, low-noise dead-reckoning KF (estim_err 0.03-0.05 m), and multi_gate is merely where dead-reckoning drift (0.5-4.3 m) finally bites — the ladder certifies a policy guaranteed to fail on the real drifting estimator; band_el 57-90 deg raises a camera-frame/tail-first mismatch question needing a one-run probe. (3) The entropy budget is consumed by three easy stages (fresh +0.30 -> -6.32 at multi_gate entry, std ~0.05) and the tanh log_std squash makes LOG_STD_MIN an absorbing state (entropy -13.676 exactly constant; gradient vanishes at the floor), so the queued entropy_weight=0.03 diagnostic cannot rescue a saturated run. On the specific questions: mid-course spawns DO exist (70% spawn 1 m before a uniform random gate — no gate-0 bottleneck), but they are trivial (inside blackout, at rest) and inflate metrics (multi_gate's 16.3% 'peak' is barely above the ~12% trivial baseline from last-gate spawns); the hover stage's seg_len override is dead code making stage 1 a duplicate of stage 2; the lookat forced-warmup-off contradiction is real in code but empirically masked because lookat almost never fires; tau_stale's 5x shift is moot today (age channel saturates at 1.0 with no fixes) but should be 0.5 everywhere; FLIGHTCHECK is max-based and near-vacuous (blackout_pass DEGRADED 0.998->0.90 during training and still passed on its inherited step-0 max, and the ladder warm-starts from the LAST checkpoint, not best — the sbatch header's 'best checkpoint' claim is false). Recommended priority order: restore dense per-gate progress on random courses (3-line reuse of the existing delta_gate) + re-init actor_logstd at stage entry, then make vision load-bearing (KF init error + realistic coast drift + perception KPIs in the advance gate), then insert a 2-gate no-stall rung (activating the identically-zero-until-now obs[13:17]) with adaptive ~300-500-update budgets and best-checkpoint selection. Per-env n_gates is not sampler-supported, but the suffix-spawn mechanism already provides per-env task-length mixing, so a short ladder with entropy management beats a long one.

Audit of the VQ2 Policy-2 (racer) RL training stack, read against the deployed pipeline (estimator_obs, frames, DiffAero source on Adroit). The multi_gate collapse is over-determined by three compounding training-mechanics defects, all fixable cheaply: (1) the tanh-squashed state-independent log_std is carried through every warm-start and by multi_gate sits near the -5 floor where the entropy bonus has a mathematically vanishing gradient — the queued entropy_weight=0.03 rerun cannot lift a saturated floor; the fix is re-initializing actor_logstd at stage boundaries plus a std floor. (2) Random-course mode has NO dense along-track progress term (R1 zeroed, R1' inert, through-centering is cross-track only); net per-step reward is negative across the 28-38.5 m inter-gate gaps, so multi-gate traversal has no gradient to follow. (3) The critic trains with an UNBOUNDED gradient (critic_grad_norm=null) at lr 2.6e-3 into a stage-changed return distribution — the 269k value_loss spike at step 100 is critic divergence, which corrupts advantages while (1) removes any recovery path. On the sim-to-deploy honesty layer, the largest optimistic gaps are: the fix surrogate hard-codes a 30 Hz detector (~25 fixes/s in-band) vs the real ~7 Hz pipeline, with no rate knob; attitude AND yaw are truth throughout obs, fix generation and KF prediction despite VQ2 having no magnetometer (yaw drifts between vision fixes at deploy); and a silent deploy contract break — stages 3-4 train obs[19] with tau_stale=0.5 while the deployed builder is test-pinned at 0.10. Medium items: KF cold-init at truth, 1-step Bernoulli stalls with teleporting age (should be a 2-state Markov burst coupled to the latency mode), no obs/return normalization, a curriculum that keeps obs[13:17] identically zero for three stages then changes five difficulty axes at once, warm-start unconditionally disabling look-at warmup even across gain changes, 70% of spawns at rest 1 m from a gate (off deploy distribution), and the perfect next-gate map (injection point for map-noise verified at peregrine_racing_inc8.py:263; fix-bias DR also under-covers the measured 0.215 m vertical bias). Verified-clean: camera intrinsics/FoV exactly match frames.py, blackout correctly gates on lagged fix geometry, action-latency DR brackets the measured 67 ms transport delay, and the env's imu config block is confirmed inert for this obs path. The forward-fuse-vs-RewindKF gap is confirmed conservative and speed-proportional — defer to the speed ramp.

Audited the inherited DiffAero trainer (algo/PPO.py, network/agents.py+networks, buffer, runner, train.py, appo.yaml via the Adroit copy) plus our full wrapper stack (rl/peregrine_train_inc8.py, peregrine_racing[_inc8].py, inc8_reward.py, inc8_estimator_emul.py, vq2_curriculum.py, peregrine_course.py, inc8_warmstart.py, the curriculum sbatch). All six required determinations are resolved with code proof: (1) NO obs normalization exists anywhere — hidden layers have post-linear LayerNorm only, which does not fix the ~400:1 per-channel scale spread that drowns the confidence triple; a fixed per-channel scale table is proposed. (2) Single Adam (lr=0.0026, eps=1e-8) over actor+logstd+critic; entropy enters the joint loss; value clip is in RAW return space with clip_coef=0.2 and max(unclipped,clipped) — with O(100-1000) returns this caps critic movement at ~0.2/update and is the direct mechanism for the multi_gate 269k value-loss spike never healing; no reward/return normalization anywhere. (3) Truncation IS bootstrapped correctly (done=terminated only, V(next_obs_before_reset) used), but the GAE λ-trace is not cut at truncations, leaking next-episode TD errors across resets. (4) actor.pth carries actor_logstd and warm-start restores it — three easy stages hand multi_gate a collapsed std≈0.05, and the tanh squash (d logstd/d param = 3.5(1-tanh²)→0) makes the floor self-locking: the queued entropy_weight=0.03 test (job 3295803) will likely fail mechanically; reset the raw logstd param at stage entry instead. (5) The privileged critic is genuinely wired at 37-d (34+triple; the '36' note was a stale docstring), but omits rates/action/time/DR-draws and suffers the same value clip. (6) Constant lr (no schedule), critic grads UNBOUNDED (critic_grad_norm=null), torch_deterministic=false, quirky best-checkpoint save that discarded this pilot's best multi_gate policy. Beyond the trainer: the requested R1'-inert verification CONFIRMS no dense forward-progress term exists in any VQ2 stage (R5'/fix_bonus survive on a per-env d2g fallback), while the GT anchor drains −2·err_ip every step — making early crashing plausibly reward-optimal in multi_gate; and the curriculum introduces the first-ever gate handoff simultaneously with 38.5 m legs that exceed the 35 m fix guard and 30 m look-at ceiling. Recommended minimal rerun recipe for multi_gate: logstd reset at stage entry + clip_value_loss=false + critic_grad_norm=5 + lr≈5e-4 + dense per-env progress term + capped GT anchor + a 2-3-gate intermediate stage with seg_len≤28; obs scale table as the next structural change.

External best-practices audit vs Swift (Kaufmann et al., Nature 2023), Song et al. (Science Robotics 2023), Rudin et al. (CoRL 2021), Andrychowicz et al. The multi_gate collapse is explained by a compound, well-documented failure: (1) exploration was exhausted before the hard stage — the state-independent tanh-squashed log_std entered multi_gate at std~0.05 and saturated at the gradient-dead LOG_STD_MIN floor (entropy -13.676 exactly), so the queued entropy_weight bump alone likely cannot recover it — a log_std RESET at each warm-start is the standard fix; (2) DiffAero PPO has NO value/return normalization and the run sets critic_grad_norm=null, so the 1-gate to 6-gate return-scale jump produced the unprotected value_loss=269k explosion at step 100 that corrupted advantages and killed the policy — add value normalization + critic grad clip + critic-only warmup; (3) the discrete warm-started stage ladder with a four-axis difficulty cliff contradicts the field-standard continuous per-env mixed-difficulty curriculum (Rudin-style), which our 2048-env setup can adopt cheaply. Supporting deltas: lr 0.0026 is ~9x the racing standard 3e-4; no observation normalization (strongest What-Matters recommendation); lookat warmup forced to 0 at boundaries; missing full previous-action in obs and Swift-style corner/rotation-matrix observations; no Swift-style empirical-residual fine-tune stage for the perfect-map/truth-attitude deploy gap. gamma=0.99/lambda=0.95 is standard and not a suspect. Top-3 actions in order: log_std reset at warm-start, value normalization + bounded critic grads + critic warmup, intra-stage mixed difficulty.
